Xiao Zhongwu only had two sons. Xiao Jing was flawless, pure, and noble; how could he be involved in such matters? If one of them had to walk this path, bearing the weight of killing, misunderstandings, infamy, and loneliness, it might as well be him.

He did not mind.

So many years had passed. He did not care about misunderstandings, nor did he fear doubt. How could one lose something they had never possessed in the first place?

Only…

Only on such a snowy day was it just too cold.

Creak—

A sound came from behind.

Xiao Jue turned around. From behind the partition door in the room, a head poked out. He Yan, leaning on her walking stick, struggled to enter, still holding his cloak.

“Sorry,” the youth said earnestly, “I knocked for a while, but you did not answer, so I…”

Xiao Jue: “So you picked the lock and invited yourself in?”

He Yan replied sheepishly, “Do not be angry; we are neighbors.” She sneezed, “Achoo—why did you not close the window? It is so cold.”

How could she say something like “we are neighbors” so casually? Xiao Jue could not be bothered to respond and closed the window.

He Yan felt wronged, too. She had knocked on the door for a long time, but Xiao Jue had not acknowledged her. She thought he was not there and figured it was just as well—better to avoid him when he was in a bad mood. So she took the chance to quietly pick the lock, slip in, leave the cloak, and leave without having to face him and think of how to comfort him.

As it turned out, he had been in the room all along. Ignoring someone like that was truly disrespectful.

“Commander, your cloak,” He Yan handed him the garment.

Xiao Jue glanced at her. “Just leave it on the couch.”

He Yan gave an “oh” and placed it on the couch, then sat down on a stool in the room. Seeing him still standing there, lost in thought, she guessed he was still upset by what Lei Hou had said in the dungeon and could not help feeling a pang of sympathy.

During her years in the Fuyue Army, she had never known that Xiao Jue had endured such hardships. If it were her, it would not matter—He Yan never considered herself special—but for something like this to happen to Xiao Jue, it felt as though fate had been too cruel.

It seemed the Heavens was not Xiao Jue’s real father either. Whatever was given, something of equal value was taken away. Worse still, it was like a shrewd merchant who never made a losing deal.

She tried to make conversation. “Commander, I must say, this cloak of yours is truly beautiful! Where did you buy it? How much did it cost?”

Xiao Jue replied, “It was bestowed by the imperial palace.”

He Yan: “…”

He was clearly unwilling to engage further, deliberately giving an answer that left no room for follow-up. He Yan hesitated, wondering if she should leave. Remembering how Xiao Jue had given her the medicine from the mandarin duck pot when she was injured, she sighed inwardly.

She was someone who repaid kindness with kindness and grudges with retribution. Now that Xiao Jue was feeling low, leaving just like that would be disloyal.

“Commander, the wound on my waist hurts so much.” He Yan changed the subject, trying to divert his attention elsewhere. “Will it leave any lasting effects?”

“Hurts?” Xiao Jue sat down at the table, his tone indifferent. “Seeing as you can still get out of bed and wander around, it should not be a big problem.”

He Yan: “…”

She said, “Commander, you should not take out your frustration with Lei Hou on me.”

Right now, he was like a firecracker, unable to hold a proper conversation.

Xiao Jue flipped through the pages of the book in front of him, not even turning his head. “You are overthinking it.”

He Yan watched him. It was likely a report from the Liangzhou Garrison about the casualties from Rida Muzi’s surprise attack. He sat at the table, carefully reviewing it.

Xiao Jue really had it tough.

He Yan thought to herself. He had first gone to Qingnan, then rushed back nonstop with the Southern Garrison Troops, then led the army to annihilate Rida Muzi’s forces, and then settled the wounded and fallen soldiers. After that, he interrogated Lei Hou and endured his taunts, and now he was back reviewing military documents without a moment’s rest.

He Yan, despite being injured, had at least managed a solid night’s sleep. But this man had not rested at all from start to finish.

Yet back in the Xianchang Academy, he had been the one who loved to slack off the most. So even Xiao Jue could not escape this fate?

His back was always as straight as a tree, as if he never grew tired, but he must feel exhaustion too.

He Yan sat on the chair, watching his back, and said, “Commander, do not take Lei Hou’s words to heart.”

Receiving no response from Xiao Jue, He Yan did not mind and continued on her own. “He’s an enemy, after all. Of course, he’d be happiest to see you angry. Everything he said was meant to provoke you. It is not just you he insulted—he insulted me too. Uh, he called me a sissy.” He Yan began to ramble again. “He also said I had hidden ailments, that my fiancée would eventually run off with someone else, that I’d end up alone, and that someday I’d be reduced to selling tofu in the east of the city with no one buying it.”

This attempt at comfort was rather clumsy. After He Yan finished speaking, even she felt it was not very thoughtful. But what else could she do? In truth, she had rarely been comforted by others, and thus, she was not very skilled at comforting others either.

Some matters simply had no clear right or wrong; one made decisions based on their position and circumstances. Outsiders could not understand the feeling of carrying everything alone—it was not a pleasant experience, and she had truly felt it herself.

So, she could also understand Xiao Jue’s feelings quite well.

Xiao Jue still could not be bothered to pay her any attention, his gaze never leaving the military documents before him.

He Yan stood up, leaning on her cane as she struggled to walk over to his side. She clenched her right hand into a fist and placed it on his desk.

“I will give you something,” she said. “I am leaving.”

She slowly dragged her steps back to her room and closed the connecting door.

After He Yan left, Xiao Jue stopped his movements and looked at the table.

Where her palm had just rested lay a sesame candy.

It looked very sweet.

CONTENT END 117

chapters.title: Chapter 118. Chu Zilan.
chapters.content:
After the incident with Rida Muzi, Liangzhou Garrison remained quite busy for a period of time.

Following the burial and erection of tombstones for the fallen recruits, their names had to be recorded in the military registry. Later, when they returned to Shuojing, bereavement allowances and compensation silver would be distributed to the families of the recruits. The fallen recruits were all scouts, mostly still very young. Having come to Liangzhou Garrison less than a year ago, their deaths left the comrades who had lived and trained with them daily feeling despondent for quite some time.

However, despite the gloom, life had to go on. Especially after this incident, Liangzhou Garrison was no longer as safe as before. Xiao Jue ordered Instructor Shen to begin drilling new formation exercises—if they truly encountered the enemy, the recruits could only achieve victory by mastering military formations.

The Southern Garrison Troops had not all arrived in Liangzhou. When Xiao Jue rushed back from Qingnan, he brought ten thousand Southern Garrison Troops with him, while the Jiuqi Battalion remained stationed in Qingnan and did not follow. Now that Liangzhou City had become a target of attention, it was truly unsuitable to draw further notice.

The daily training of the Southern Garrison Troops differed from that of the Liangzhou Garrison. As Xiao Jue had said, the duration and intensity of their daily drills were three times that of Liangzhou Garrison. Whenever the recruits of Liangzhou Garrison witnessed the vigor of the Southern Garrison Troops during training, they could not help but sigh in admiration.

For a time, the previously spacious martial arts field became bustling. At the foot of Baiyue Mountain and along the banks of the Wulu River, soldiers could be seen everywhere.

He Yan’s injuries were also gradually healing day by day.

Lin Shuanghe’s medical skills were far more refined than Shen Muxue’s. Initially, it was thought that such injuries would take at least a year or more to recover from, but at this rate, in another two months, He Yan felt she could even bounce around energetically on the martial arts field again.

Song Taotao placed a bowl of soup in front of He Yan and, after watching her finish it, took the bowl and left. The young lady could not cook herself, so she relied on her status as a young mistress to “raid” the kitchen soldiers for food to feed He Yan. Sometimes, He Yan could not help but feel as if she were freeloading, but after the initial awkwardness, she grew accustomed to it.

After all, the soup was delicious. It would have been even better if the young lady did not look at her with the kind of gaze one reserves for a treasure.

From the other end of the room, faint voices could be heard, seemingly Liang Ping’s, and he sounded somewhat agitated.

He Yan thought for a moment on the bed, then got up, leaning on a stick as she stepped down.

She took out the silver wire from her sleeve and inserted it into the lock. Having picked locks many times, she was now quite adept at it. Fortunately, Xiao Jue turned a blind eye to such behavior and had not replaced the lock with a more complex “士”-shaped one. Presumably, Xiao Jue’s important documents were not kept in this room, which explained the lax security.

He Yan pushed the connecting door open a crack and saw someone kneeling before Xiao Jue—it was Du Mao, whom she had not seen in a long time. Since the incident with Rida Muzi, Lei Hou’s identity as a spy had been exposed. As Lei Hou’s relative and the one who had recommended him, Du Mao had disappeared without a trace. According to Cheng Lisu, Du Mao seemed to have been imprisoned. He Yan could understand this—since Lei Hou was a traitor, no one could guarantee Du Mao’s innocence.

Now that Du Mao appeared here, it was likely his innocence had been proven.

In the room, besides the kneeling Du Mao, stood a group of instructors. He Yan saw Liang Ping step forward and plead, “Commander, Drillmaster Du had not seen Lei Hou for many years. He truly had no knowledge of Lei Hou being a spy. Please show mercy, Commander.”

“Yes, Commander,” Ma Damei could not help but speak up. “Drillmaster Du has been at Liangzhou Garrison for ten years and has never made a single mistake. If Lei Hou had not deliberately concealed the truth, things would not have come to this. Please, Commander, consider Drillmaster Du’s years of hard work and show leniency in his punishment.”

The other instructors all echoed her plea, interceding on Du Mao’s behalf.

Du Mao had come to Liangzhou Garrison in his twenties, enduring the harsh, cold land for a full decade. Day after day at the garrison offered little amusement—at most, the instructors would gather to drink during festivals. His daily routine consisted of either training soldiers or guarding the territory.

The instructors shared a deep bond and naturally could not bear to see Du Mao lose his life because of Lei Hou’s actions. Out of compassion, they had come to plead for mercy.

Shen Han moved his lips but ultimately said nothing. It was not that he lacked affection for Du Mao, but even after less than a year of interaction, Shen Han understood that the Second Young Master Xiao before them was not one to change his mind based on others’ words.

Sure enough, Xiao Jue ignored the others’ appeals and looked directly at Du Mao, asking, “What do you intend to do?”

He Yan still remembered when she first arrived at Liangzhou Garrison. This instructor, named Du Mao, had been quite close to Liang Ping, often bickering with him. Among the instructors, he was relatively young. Yet now, after just a few short days, he seemed to have aged ten years, with scattered strands of white hair at his temples and a much wearier expression.

Du Mao spoke, his tone heavy with exhaustion: “Du Mao is willing to accept punishment.”

“Du Mao!” Liang Ping cried out anxiously.

“It was my negligence not to verify Lei Hou’s current status before rashly recommending him for the garrison. This is a dereliction of duty,” Du Mao said. “The Commander’s punishment is justified.”

“You were indeed derelict in your duty,” Xiao Jue stated calmly. “Because of you, many new recruits at Liangzhou Garrison lost their lives.”

The instructors who had been about to continue pleading froze, not daring to speak further.

“The dead will not return to life,” Xiao Jue said. “Do you understand?”

“Du Mao understands.”

The room fell silent. Liang Ping looked at Du Mao with despair in his eyes.

“I will not take your life.”

At these words, everyone in the room was stunned, including He Yan.

Xiao Jue said, “Leave.”

“Commander…”

“From today onward, you are no longer an instructor at Liangzhou Garrison.” Xiao Jue stood up and walked toward the door. “Do not return in the future.”

His figure disappeared outside. After a moment of silence in the room, Ma Damei snapped back to reality and went to pull Du Mao, who was still kneeling on the ground. “Alright, alright, the Commander has shown you mercy. Get up now.”

Du Mao stood there dazed, then suddenly broke into loud sobs.

The comforting words of the others in the room, mingled with Du Mao’s weeping, gave He Yan a headache. She grabbed her coat, draped it over her shoulders, and, leaning on her walking stick, followed them out the door. As soon as she stepped outside, the wind and snow made her shiver.

Where was Xiao Jue? He Yan looked around. The man had just left—how could he have vanished so quickly? Could he fly?

“Looking for me?” A voice came from behind her, startling He Yan so much she nearly dropped her walking stick.

She turned around to see Xiao Jue standing behind her, raising an eyebrow as he stared at her. “Something the matter?”

“N-no, nothing,” He Yan replied, pretending to gaze at the sky. “The weather is nice. I just came out for a walk.”

Xiao Jue glanced at the sand-like snowflakes outside and mocked, “I thought you had not eavesdropped enough earlier and wanted to ask me something yourself.”

He actually knew she was eavesdropping? This was awkward. He Yan scratched her head. “Your Excellency has sharp ears.”

Xiao Jue curved his lips. “Not as sharp as yours.”

“Speak,” he asked. “What do you want from me?”

What did she want from him? He Yan did not know either; she had just instinctively followed him out. She was at a loss for words for a moment, then thought about it and said, “Your Excellency, you still showed mercy toward Drillmaster Du.”

The drillmasters’ close personal relationship with Du Mao was one thing, but Du Mao’s own mistakes were another. He Yan had thought that, given Xiao Jue’s temperament, Du Mao would not escape death. Unexpectedly, in the end, he was only expelled from the Liangzhou Garrison.

Xiao Jue smiled, as if finding her words amusing. “Showed mercy?”

“Yes, if it were me…”

“If it were you, what would you do?”

He Yan suddenly could not speak.

What would she do if it were her? From a common soldier to deputy general to general, she had encountered such situations before. In truth, General Feihong’s governance was not much more lenient than Xiao Jue’s. However, most of the time, others instinctively overlooked this, simply because she usually mingled with her subordinates and did not have the same “remarkable achievements” of being aloof and unfeeling as Xiao Jue.

If it were her, would she order Du Mao’s life to be taken?

“If it were me, I would not either,” He Yan said. “Taking Du Mao’s life may seem like strict military discipline, but in reality, it wounds people’s hearts. The Liangzhou Garrison has just gone through the incident with Rida Muzi. If morale collapses, the Liangzhou Garrison will be like scattered sand, difficult to hold together.”

Xiao Jue looked at her with a hint of surprise in his gaze. “Well said.”

He Yan said proudly, “I told you before, I am number one in the Liangzhou Garrison. I am very clever. So, Your Excellency, can you let me into the Jiuqi Battalion?”

Xiao Jue curved the corner of his mouth. “No.”

This man was truly stubborn. He Yan was about to argue further on her own behalf when she saw him turn and continue walking forward. He Yan leaned on her crutch and followed, asking, “Where are you going, Your Excellency?”

“The martial arts field.”

“Going to watch the training?” He Yan said. “I will go too!”

After being injured, she naturally could not participate in the daily training. Every day, aside from lying in bed, she would only hobble a few circles outside with her crutch. It was truly boring. Even though Song Taotao and Cheng Lisu would find opportunities to come and chat with her, these two—one only remembered trivial matters like which young lady in the capital was beautiful or which lady had just given birth to a son, and the other knew nothing besides eating, drinking, and having fun—made conversation with them exhausting. The only one she could still talk to, Lin Shuanghe, had been invited by Shen Muxue to help brew medicine for the injured soldiers at the medical clinic.

Therefore, when Xiao Jue mentioned going to the martial arts field, He Yan felt a stirring of excitement.

The snow had lightened, and it was not as cold outside as before. He Yan could not walk fast with her crutch and complained, “Your Excellency, wait for me!”

Such a presumptuous tone made Xiao Jue’s footsteps pause involuntarily. He retorted, “Am I your servant?”

“No,” He Yan came to her senses and explained, “I mean, we could walk a bit slower and chat about something else. Ahem, did Lei Hou say anything about why Rida Muzi came to our garrison to cause trouble? The Western Qiang rebellion was already quelled by General Feihong, was it not? Where did the Qiang tribe get so many soldiers?”

Tens of thousands of soldiers—did the Qiang tribe truly have so many troops now? Having fought against Rida Muji before, He Yan was all too familiar with the Qiang tribe’s situation, and something felt off.

“It’s not the Qiang tribe,” Xiao Jue answered He Yan’s question, a rare occurrence. “It’s the Wutu people.”

“The Wutu people?” This time, He Yan was genuinely taken aback.

Xiao Jue glanced at her, taking in her surprised expression, and said calmly, “What are your thoughts?”

Was he testing her? He Yan asked, “Is Rida Muzi a Wutu person?”

Xiao Jue was silent for a moment before replying, “He is not a Wutu person, but aside from Rida Muzi and a few of his close associates you’ve fought before, the rest of the soldiers are all Wutu people.”

“Are you absolutely certain, Commander?”

Xiao Jue continued walking unhurriedly. “Certain.”

“If it truly is the Wutu people,” He Yan’s voice grew serious, “then what they seek is not just the Liangzhou Garrison.”

“What do you mean?”

“In recent years, the Wutu Kingdom has been raising armies, building formidable strength, and frequently harassing civilians at the border, clearly testing the waters. Now, coming to the Liangzhou Garrison under the guise of the Qiang tribe, they hide in the shadows, intending to wreak havoc in Great Wei under the Qiang tribe’s name.”

“Consider this, Commander: if you had truly gone to Zhangtai and failed to provide timely aid, and the Wutu people had seized the Liangzhou Garrison, then taken the city, occupying Liangzhou would be like tearing a breach in Great Wei’s border. They could march westward unimpeded, following the river all the way to the capital.”

Xiao Jue raised his eyes. “Is that all?”

“Great Wei likely has a traitor colluding with the enemy,” He Yan said. “This person has secret dealings with the Wutu people and is an old acquaintance of yours, Commander.”

Xiao Jue said, “Go on.”

“To plant trusted agents in the Liangzhou Garrison without detection and spread false information from Zhangtai, this person must hold a high position and have extensive connections. Knowing that the Liangzhou Garrison is impregnable with you here, they first lured you away—this person must fear you greatly. Therefore,” He Yan looked at Xiao Jue, “there might be someone with high status in the court who has clashed with you in the past but gained no advantage. If such a person exists, it is almost certainly them.”

Xiao Jue’s gaze fixed on her, and he said bluntly, “Then why not tell me who this person is?”

Now, He Yan felt utterly baffled. Though she and Xiao Jue had been classmates, it was only for a year. After that, they had not seen each other for many years—one was in the south, the other in the north. Xiao Jue, embroiled in court intrigues due to Xiao Zhongwu’s affairs, was deeply involved, while she, innocent and relying solely on military merits for promotion, spent her days in border camps. Thus, she knew little about the messy affairs of the court. How could she guess who that person was?

Even if this was a test, it was too difficult. Not everyone was like him, able to sleep their way to the top of the Xianchang Academy.

Recalling the incident with Yuan Baozhen, He Yan said casually, “Xu Jingfu?”

Xiao Jue was taken aback.

Seeing his expression, He Yan’s heart stirred. “Is it really him?”

Xiao Jue did not answer.

“Xu Jingfu is colluding with the enemy and betraying the country?” He Yan exclaimed in shock. “He’s gone mad! He’s the current prime minister—what benefit could he possibly gain from this?”

“You could speak a little louder,” Xiao Jue said indifferently. “Without evidence, you could be accused of slandering a court official at any moment.”

He Yan thought to herself, “Who was not a court official?” In her past life as General Feihong, she too had been on the imperial payroll.

“But, but…” she wanted to say more, but Xiao Jue had already stopped walking and looked ahead. Not far away, the low shouts of soldiers forming ranks could be heard.

Unconsciously, the two of them had arrived at the martial arts field.

Originally, the martial arts field was only used for daily training by the Liangzhou Garrison recruits. Now, it was divided into eastern and western sections. The eastern side was where the Southern Garrison Troops were drilling, while the western side belonged to the Liangzhou Garrison. At this moment, with both sides training simultaneously, the difference became apparent.

The deputy commander of the Southern Garrison Troops was drilling his soldiers in formation. No one needed to give orders; just watching them made one feel their fierce and invincible spirit. Meanwhile, the Liangzhou Garrison recruits had only just begun learning how to form ranks, inevitably appearing somewhat flustered. Shen Han stood on the high platform, shouting at the top of his lungs.

He Yan watched for a while, then hesitantly said, “Are they practicing… the Fish Scale Formation?”

Xiao Jue glanced at her sideways and asked, “You know about it?”

“Here we go again; he’s testing people once more.” Although He Yan was somewhat puzzled by Xiao Jue’s occasional questions, she thought perhaps he was preparing to test her ability to join the Jiuqi Battalion. So she answered earnestly, “Distributed in tiers, slightly convex at the front, with the main force concentrated in the center, then divided into several small fish-scale-like formations. When facing the enemy, it can concentrate forces to launch a fierce attack on the enemy’s center, but its weakness lies in the flanks. If the enemy breaks through from the flanks, they can break this formation. It is indeed the Fish Scale Formation, but…” she added, “They are too loose.”

Too loose! If they took this long to form up properly, they would have been killed five times over.

Xiao Jue looked at her thoughtfully, then suddenly curled his lips into a smile. “Not bad.”

He Yan felt proud. Hard work truly paid off. Who would have thought that the last-place student from the Xianchang Academy back then would now have military tactics memorized by heart? Even when facing questions from the academy’s top student, she could answer with ease. All those years of fighting and studying had not been in vain—it was enough.

“Studied military tactics?” Xiao Jue raised an eyebrow.

“I know a little.”

“Know how to set up formations?”

“I would not dare claim that.”

“Alright,” Xiao Jue looked down at the soldiers drilling below and said, “If Rida Muzi had come to the Liangzhou Garrison that day, and you had not been locked in the dungeon, and Shen Han had handed command over to you, how would you have fought this battle?”

So soon with the test questions?

He Yan pondered for a moment, then slowly replied, “Those Wutu people are strong, well-equipped, fierce, and brutal. The Liangzhou Garrison recruits have never been on the battlefield before; their morale is low, and they cannot withstand a direct confrontation. It is also not something that can be resolved in a short time. If it were me… I would use the Chariot Wheel Formation.”

Xiao Jue watched her quietly. “Go on.”

“As the commander, I would position myself in the center of the formation to hold the line, with outer forces deployed in layers. I would disperse the troops outward to form mobile formations. During battle, they would rotate in the same direction, taking turns attacking the enemy formation, like a turning wheel. This way, constant pressure would be applied to one part of the enemy forces. The Wutu people would collapse from exhaustion, while our side would take turns attacking, allowing us to replenish, rest, and recover our combat strength.”

“You as the commander?” Xiao Jue mocked.

“What I mean is, I would temporarily act as the commander to hold the line. The one who really needs to fight is still you, Commander. The reason for choosing the Chariot Wheel Formation is also to buy time so that you, Commander, could return in time to provide support.” He Yan spoke very earnestly.

Xiao Jue turned around, slightly leaning down as he lowered his eyes to look at her, a faint smile curling his lips. “Young Lady He has studied military strategy quite well. It would be a pity if you did not become a general.”

No matter what else could be said about Xiao Jue, his judgment was quite sharp. He Yan nodded. “I think so too. I feel I was born to be a general. Sometimes I even think I was a female general in my past life.”

Xiao Jue: “…”

“You do not believe me, Commander?” He Yan poked a hole in the snow with her stick. “Or do you think women cannot be generals?”

“I never thought that.”

He Yan looked up at him. Most people believed women should stay in their chambers, embroidering or applying makeup, waiting for their husband’s favor. Not to mention becoming a female general, even appearing in public as a shopkeeper, teacher, or physician would draw many strange looks.

Very few dared to take that step, and even if they did, they rarely gained others’ understanding.

“You can do whatever you want,” the young man said lazily, a slight tug at the corner of his mouth. “As long as you can achieve it.”

He Yan was taken aback, staring at him without a word.

His gaze drifted toward the distant martial arts field, settling on the drilling recruits, unaware that He Yan’s eyes were fixed on his back.

“Thank you,” He Yan whispered in her heart.

The snow gradually stopped. The recruits led by Shen Han had practiced several times and were growing more proficient, no longer as flustered as before. The formation was beginning to take shape, and Xiao Jue and He Yan had been standing there for quite some time.

A familiar voice sounded from behind. “Huaijin! He… brother!”

He Yan turned to see Lin Shuanghe. He climbed up to the pavilion, brushing the snow off his boots. “No wonder I could not find you two anywhere. So you are here. What’s going on?” He looked at Xiao Jue with a teasing smile. “Bringing our Little Sister He to watch the drills?”

He Yan: “… Physician Lin, please do not call me ‘little sister’ in public.”

“My apologies.” Lin Shuanghe covered his mouth with his fan, looking regretful. “I forgot for a moment. But there are no outsiders here anyway.” He glanced at the stick He Yan was leaning on and asked, “Can you walk this far from bed today? How is it? Does the wound still hurt?”

“Not too much,” He Yan replied. “Physician Lin’s medical skills are exceptional. I am feeling much better today.”

“That’s wonderful.” Lin Shuanghe waved his fan. “If I could not heal you, I’d feel terribly guilty.”

As the two exchanged compliments, Xiao Jue watched coldly from the side, seemingly unable to bear it any longer. Impatiently, he said, “If you have something to say, say it.”

Lin Shuanghe paused. “Ah! I almost forgot the main thing. Someone just arrived at the Liangzhou Garrison. I wanted to find Instructor Shen, but he was not around. I searched for a long time before finding you here.”

“Who is it?”

“Someone from the palace. They said His Majesty has sent rewards for the great victory of the Liangzhou Garrison. Oh, and also… that…” He struggled to recall the name, pausing for a moment before remembering. “The Fourth Young Master from the Earl of Shijin’s residence, Chu Zilan! Yes, Chu Zilan is here too.”

“Chu Zhao?” Xiao Jue frowned. “What is he doing here?”

Lin Shuanghe shrugged. “How should I know? They are all waiting at the garrison gate. Are you not going to see them?”

Xiao Jue hesitated briefly before heading down. “Let’s go.”

“Hey, Commander, what about me?” He Yan hurriedly leaned on her stick, wanting to follow, but she was not sure if she was allowed to in such a situation. Judging by Xiao Jue’s demeanor, it did not seem like a casual reunion between old friends.

Xiao Jue glanced at her and said, “Go back. There’s no need to follow.”

“Oh,” He Yan obediently agreed. Lin Shuanghe waved at her, and the two quickly descended the pavilion, their figures disappearing into the distance.

He Yan gazed at the vast snowy landscape, a hint of doubt stirring in her heart.

Who exactly was this person called Chu Zilan?

CONTENT END 118

chapters.title: Chapter 119. Old Friend.
chapters.content:
Outside the garrison stood a group of people.

Servants by the carriage were busy unloading trunks from the vehicle. In the resting area near the garrison entrance, guests were seated, drinking tea.

The moment Xiao Jue entered, he saw Liang Ping pouring tea for someone.

“Fourth Young Master Chu,” Lin Shuanghe was the first to greet, stepping forward with a fan in hand and smiling as familiarly as a host entertaining guests. “I hope the tea suits your taste?”

Chu Zilan stood up and cupped his hands toward Lin Shuanghe and Xiao Jue. “General Xiao, Young Master Lin,” he smiled. “The Yunwu tea of Liangzhou Garrison is mellow, bright, and elegant, leaving a lingering fragrance on the palate. The Commander has excellent taste.”

Xiao Jue casually pulled over a chair, sat down, and stared at him. “Just coarse tea, no need for such courtesy.”

Chu Zhao was not offended; he merely smiled as he replied, “The Commander jests.”

The fourth son of the Earl of Shijin’s household was the same age as Xiao Jue. Compared to Xiao Jue’s often indifferent and weary expression, he appeared much gentler. He was also exceptionally handsome, with refined features, fair skin, and a jade-colored, loose robe that made him look even more slender and ethereal. His eyes were narrow and long, always carrying a hint of a smile—truly a graceful gentleman, gentle as jade.

The two of them together, one as cold and aloof as autumn water, the other as pure and bright as an orchid, made for a pleasing sight.

Beside Chu Zhao stood a young woman dressed as a maid. Though clad in simple servant’s attire, she was strikingly beautiful, with deep, radiant features that even plain clothing could not conceal. Even Lin Shuanghe, who was accustomed to seeing beauties, could not help but glance at her a few more times, inwardly marveling that this master and servant standing together seemed even less like ordinary mortals. Among the Earl of Shijin’s four sons, the first three were plain in appearance, while only this one had grown into such a striking figure—a testament to the importance of maternal beauty.

“What brings Fourth Young Master Chu to Liangzhou Garrison?” Xiao Jue asked.

Chu Zhao smiled and replied, “His Majesty heard that General Xiao annihilated tens of thousands of enemy troops in Liangzhou Garrison and eradicated the remnants of the Qiang tribe. He was overjoyed and specifically sent me to deliver rewards, as well as to observe the morale of Liangzhou Garrison’s formidable troops.”

“Delivering rewards?” Xiao Jue looked at him with amusement, speaking nonchalantly. “Liangzhou is a harsh and bitter land. For Fourth Young Master Chu to condescend to visit and observe,” he smiled slightly, “is no small matter.”

Chu Zhao said, “To witness the formidable troops led by General Xiao in person is Zilan’s good fortune.”

Xiao Jue chuckled but did not respond.

“For this great victory in Liangzhou, His Majesty also ordered me to host a celebration banquet here,” Chu Zhao continued. “However, I am not familiar with how Liangzhou Garrison typically celebrates victories, so I must trouble the Commander with the arrangements.”

“The newly fallen soldiers have just been buried,” Xiao Jue said. “Holding a celebration now might not be appropriate.”

Chu Zhao’s smile remained gentle, but his tone was firm. “In war, how can there be no bloodshed? Moreover, annihilating the enemy is a joyous occasion. Rewards should be given where they are due—this is also His Majesty’s intention.”

Was he invoking Emperor Wenxuan now?

Xiao Jue stared at him for a while before finally nodding and smiling. “Very well.” He stood up and said meaningfully, “The celebration banquet can be held tomorrow. I invite Fourth Young Master Chu to join us.”

Chu Zhao rose and returned the courtesy. “I dare not refuse such an honor.”

Xiao Jue left the room and instructed Fei Nu, “Arrange rooms for Fourth Young Master Chu’s people.”

Fei Nu accepted the order and departed.

Lin Shuanghe followed him out, sidled up to him, and asked in a low voice, “What is Chu Zhao here for? From the looks of it, he intends to stay at Liangzhou Garrison for a while?”

“With the person gone, Xu Jingfu is anxious,” Xiao Jue replied calmly. “He sent his dog over to take a look. Is there a problem?”

Lin Shuanghe glanced back at the room, where Chu Zhao was sipping tea with his head lowered, and asked, “Is it safe to let him stay here? After all, this guy is Xu Jingfu’s man.”

“Safe?” Xiao Jue said. “That depends on his capabilities. Let’s go.”

“Where to?”

“Since it is a reward, we should see what’s in it,” Xiao Jue spoke with a hint of amusement. “Coming to my Liangzhou Garrison with such fanfare—just a few crates of rewards seems rather inadequate.”

“You are going to pluck feathers from a passing goose again?”

Xiao Jue shot him a glance.

Lin Shuanghe said, “No other meaning, just asking. Do not be angry. Let’s go; let’s go see the treasures!”

…

He Yan returned from the martial arts field and found herself idle once again. She lay in bed reading a few travelogues, waiting for Song Taotao to bring her meal. After eating, as Song Taotao was leaving, she heard movement outside the door, as if Song Taotao was talking to someone. Thinking it was Xiao Jue returning, she propped herself up with a stick, got out of bed, and opened the door, only to see Lin Shuanghe.

“Physician Lin?” He Yan looked around but did not see Xiao Jue, so she asked, “Is the Commander not here?”

“He went to discuss the victory banquet with the drillmaster,” Lin Shuanghe said with a smile. “I will wait for him in his room first. I still have something to discuss with him.”

“Victory banquet?” He Yan was momentarily confused. “What victory banquet?”

“The Liangzhou Garrison victory banquet.” Lin Shuanghe waved to Song Taotao, and after she left, he walked toward He Yan. But as he reached the doorway, he suddenly stopped and refused to go any further.

He Yan was puzzled. “What’s wrong?”

Lin Shuanghe withdrew his hand and said seriously, “It’s improper for a man and a woman to be alone in the same room. If word got out, it would damage your reputation.”

He Yan: “…”

She said, “No one here knows my identity, Physician Lin. You can just treat me like an ordinary recruit. Besides, have you not been here before?”

Lin Shuanghe waved his hand reservedly. “There were other people in the room before, but now it is just the two of us. I am afraid it might cause misunderstandings.”

“What misunderstandings?” He Yan said helplessly. “The Commander and I are often alone in the same room, and nothing improper has ever happened.”

Hearing this, Lin Shuanghe took another step back. “That makes it even more inappropriate. ‘A friend’s wife is not to be trifled with.’ How could I be the kind of scoundrel who betrays a friend?”

He Yan: “…”

What nonsense was this person spouting?

After some thought, she finally came up with a good solution. “How about this, Young Master Lin? You go to the Commander’s room, and I will stay in mine. I will open the connecting door, and we can talk through it. That way, we will not be in the same room but in two separate rooms. Is that acceptable?”

Lin Shuanghe had not expected He Yan to come up with such an idea. After a moment of surprise, he slapped his fan and said, “Let’s do it!”

So, after He Yan returned to her room, used Cheng Lisu’s silver wire to pick the lock, and laboriously pushed a stool to the other side of the connecting door, Lin Shuanghe was already waiting there.

He examined the connecting door and asked He Yan, “Do you two usually play like this?”

“Play like what?”

“I mean…” Lin Shuanghe trailed off, seeming to feel a bit embarrassed himself. He shook his head and laughed. “I never thought Huaijin would be like this…”

He Yan was baffled by his words but still remembered the matter of the victory banquet he had mentioned earlier, so she asked, “Physician Lin, what is this Liangzhou Garrison victory banquet you just spoke of?”

“Did you not all defeat Rida Muzi’s forces earlier, wiping out tens of thousands of enemy troops?” Lin Shuanghe replied. “When His Majesty heard of this, he was greatly pleased. He specifically sent someone to bring rewards and commendations, and even ordered a victory banquet to be held at Liangzhou Garrison to honor the three armies.”

Upon hearing this, He Yan was stunned. “Now? Holding a victory banquet now does not seem appropriate.”

Celebrating a victory at Liangzhou Garrison at this moment was hardly a good idea. Although they had won the battle, it had come hastily. At the outset, dozens of scouts had died without knowing the full situation. Even though they ultimately prevailed, it was largely due to the support of the Southern Garrison Troops. At this moment, the new recruits were likely feeling more sorrow for their fallen comrades and fear of war than the joy of victory. How could a celebration be fitting now?

“What can be done about His Majesty’s decree?” Lin Shuanghe sighed. “Can we afford to be ungrateful?”

For a moment, neither of them spoke.

After a while, He Yan asked, “The person who came to deliver His Majesty’s decree—is that the Chu Zilan you mentioned today?” She continued, “Who is Chu Zilan?”

“You’ve never heard of Chu Zilan?” This time, Lin Shuanghe was genuinely surprised.

He Yan shook her head.

“Among the dream lovers of young women in the capital, Xiao Jing ranks first, Xiao Huaijin ranks second, and Chu Zilan ranks third,” Lin Shuanghe remarked with a sigh. “But ever since Xiao Jing got married, only Xiao Huaijin and Chu Zilan remain. Our Huaijin is aloof by nature and does not enjoy speaking with young ladies, so in recent years, he has fallen behind Chu Zilan in popularity. Although Chu Zilan’s background is somewhat humble, he is exceptionally handsome, gentle, and amiable, and he is still unmarried. If you ask the women of the capital who they would most like to marry, nine out of ten would name Chu Zilan.” He looked at He Yan. “When you were in the capital before, did you not hear his name? That’s impossible, is it not?”

He Yan, of course, had no idea. She had been busy leading troops and fighting battles, with no time to concern herself with romantic affairs or the handsome men of the capital. Later, after returning to the capital and quickly marrying, she had no opportunity to learn about men outside her household. She truly had never heard of this Chu Zilan.

“I was raised in seclusion by my father since childhood, rarely leaving the inner chambers and seldom speaking with men outside the family,” He Yan said earnestly, though casually. “I truly know nothing about such matters.”

“Is that so?” Lin Shuanghe said. “Then your father really did keep you under strict supervision.”

He Yan nodded. “Indeed.” She then asked, “What is the relationship between this Chu Zilan and General Xiao?”

Xiao Jue was a person who, though not particularly close to anyone, had never shown any special fondness for anyone, nor had he ever displayed any particular dislike for anyone. Xu Jingfu was one exception, and this Chu Zilan—though they had not even met today, merely hearing his name seemed to displease Xiao Jue.

Could there have been some past conflict?

“That’s a long story,” Lin Shuanghe said, rising to pour himself a cup of tea from the small table. After taking a sip to moisten his throat, he sat back down and said to He Yan, “You may not have heard of Chu Zilan, but have you heard of his father, Earl of Shijin Chu Linfeng?”

He Yan felt the name sounded somewhat familiar. After a moment of thought, she said, “Is he the one who married nineteen concubines, each one a stunning beauty?”

“Exactly!”

He Yan remembered the name Chu Linfeng. Back in the military days, when the deputy generals and their subordinates gathered to chat, they did not envy the emperor—the person they envied most was this Earl of Shijin. The Earl of Shijin was as handsome as a jade tree in the wind, a famously handsome man in Great Wei, yet the wife he married was several years older than him, famously ugly, and fierce-tempered.

A libertine like Chu Linfeng would never have given up. Before marriage, he spent his days lingering in pleasure quarters, and after marriage, he became even worse. The wife he married was virtuous and gentle, seemingly aware of her plain looks and lack of favor from her husband, so she never stopped him from taking concubines. Over the years, he had taken nineteen concubines, each as beautiful as flowers, capable of making fish sink and geese fall, each with their own charm.

But taking concubines was one thing—over all these years, aside from the three young masters born from his wife, not a single concubine had ever borne Earl of Shijin’s child.

It was said that before these concubines entered the Chu family, they were forced to take infertility medicine. No matter how favored they were, without children, aside from pleasing their master, they could only please the mistress. The Earl of Shijin’s Madam kept these concubines firmly under her thumb, and none dared to cause trouble under her watch. Earl of Shijin continued to dote on his concubines every day, while Earl of Shijin’s Madam simply pretended not to see it, focusing on raising her three sons.

Chu Zilan was Earl of Shijin’s fourth son, but he was not born to the Earl of Shijin’s Madam.

“Is he a son born to a concubine?” He Yan asked.

“No, no,” Lin Shuanghe said. “Madam Chu managed the concubines more strictly than your father managed you. How could a concubine possibly give birth to a son?”

“Then…”

“I do not know the specifics, but one day, during a Chu family banquet, a four-year-old son suddenly appeared, named Chu Zhao.” Lin Shuanghe took another sip of tea. “Though no one said it outright, everyone understood: this Chu Zhao was likely Chu Linfeng’s illegitimate son born to an outside kept woman.”

He Yan’s eyes widened.

“Madam Chu guarded against everything but never expected the Earl of Shijin to have such a trick up his sleeve. The child was already four years old, acknowledged in front of everyone—what could she do?” Lin Shuanghe spread his hands. “If that were all, Chu Zilan would merely be Chu Linfeng’s illegitimate son. But when Chu Zilan turned ten, he was registered under Madam Chu’s name, so now, his status is that of the legitimate Fourth Young Master of the Earl of Shijin estate. Do you know why?”

“Why?”

“Because he is the most favored student of the current Prime Minister, Xu Jingfu.”

He Yan was taken aback—Xu Jingfu again?

“Though the Earl of Shijin was a libertine and not a particularly kind father, life under Madam Chu could not have been easy for Chu Zilan. I do not know how he managed to survive safely until the age of ten and then how he connected with Xu Jingfu. How could the Earl of Shijin dare to disregard the Prime Minister’s face? Later, registering Chu Zhao under Madam Chu’s name was likely Xu Jingfu’s idea.”

“So this Fourth Young Master Chu is quite impressive.”

Lin Shuanghe looked at He Yan. “Do you think he’s impressive?”

“Impressive. As you said, he had no external support in the estate—his father did not care for him, and his birth mother was not by his side, yet he became a legitimate young master and even had the Emperor send him to Liangzhou Garrison to deliver an edict. To have come this far on his own is truly remarkable.”

“If he were not impressive, how could he have become Xu Jingfu’s favorite student?” Lin Shuanghe shook his head and sighed.

“What about his birth mother?” He Yan asked. “Was she not taken into the Earl of Shijin’s residence?”

“I do not know.” Lin Shuanghe shook his head. “I heard she fell ill and passed away after giving birth to him. If not for that, given Chu Zilan’s current abilities, he could have provided her a better life.”

He Yan nodded thoughtfully. “I see. No wonder General Xiao dislikes Fourth Young Master Chu.”

Xiao Jue and Xu Jingfu were enemies rather than friends. Since Chu Zilan was Xu Jingfu’s student, he naturally became Xiao Jue’s enemy as well.

“He… Brother He,” Lin Shuanghe said, “If you had to choose between Huaijin and Chu Zilan, who would you side with?”

He Yan found the question utterly baffling. “Why do you ask?”

“I am just curious about what the young ladies of Great Wei would choose.”

“I do not even know Chu Zilan,” He Yan replied. “Of course I’d stand with the Commander.”

Lin Shuanghe then revealed a meaningful smile. “No need to answer so quickly. At tomorrow’s victory banquet, you will get to meet Chu Zilan.”

He Yan: “…”

What difference would meeting him make? Was there something special about him?

He Yan had not expected that, just as Lin Shuanghe said, she would indeed meet this legendary figure the very next day—the man who haunted the dreams of Great Wei’s young maidens, the one said to rival Xiao Jue: Fourth Young Master Chu, Chu Zilan.

…

That night, it surprisingly did not snow, and the following day turned out to be clear and sunny.

Though the weather remained cold, the sunlight shining on people brought a comforting warmth. When He Yan got up to drink her porridge, she felt that under the sun’s rays, the wound on her waist seemed to heal faster. Liangzhou Garrison truly was peculiar—in summer, people complained bitterly about the scorching heat and cursed the sun, yet in winter, they rejoiced at even half a day of sunshine.

Unable to participate in the daily training at the martial arts field but finding the sunlight too pleasant to waste, He Yan decided to take her cane and stroll around the courtyard. Just as she reached the entrance, she heard Song Taotao’s voice declaring, “I saw this golden cake roll first! It is mine!”

This was followed by a woman’s patient voice: “Young lady, this was specially made by our young master’s personal chef. It did not come from the guard’s kitchen, so it is not yours.”

“You say it is your young master’s, so it must be?” the girl angrily retorted. “It’s placed in the kitchen—how am I supposed to know if your chef made it? Since you have your own chef, can you not just make another one?”

“The golden cake roll requires complicated preparation. Making another would delay our young master’s meal.”

“Then do not eat it!”

“Young lady…”

He Yan could not listen any longer and stepped out. “Young Lady Song.”

Song Taotao turned, along with the woman she was arguing with, and exclaimed joyfully, “Brother He! This is a golden cake roll. Would you like to try it?”

He Yan: “…”

The woman also spoke up: “That belongs to our young master…”

He Yan took the golden cake roll and returned it to the woman. “Please do not mind her—she’s just a child who does not know better.”

“Brother He!” Song Taotao stamped her foot in frustration. “Why did you give it back to her?”

“It was theirs to begin with.” He Yan shook her head. She guessed that the “young master” the woman referred to must be that Fourth Young Master of the Earl of Shijin’s residence, Chu Zilan. Given the delicate relationship between Chu Zilan and Xiao Jue, causing trouble for Xiao Jue over this would be more trouble than it was worth.

“Thank you, young master.” The woman smiled gracefully at He Yan.

He Yan was also taken aback for a moment, startled by the girl’s appearance. There were already few women in the Liangzhou Garrison, and aside from her, the fake one, there were only Shen Muxue and Song Taotao. One was elegant and refined, the other cute and lively. Now, with this peony-like beauty appearing, she stood out even more.

Even Chu Zilan’s maidservant was this beautiful? He Yan thought to herself. Before, Lin Shuanghe had said that among the women of Great Wei, the ranking for ideal husbands placed Chu Zilan first. Only a fool would choose Chu Zilan. If even his maidservant was such a stunning beauty, how could ordinary women ever catch his eye? It would be better to choose Xiao Jue. Xiao Jue was always surrounded by men, and perhaps after seeing so many men, his standards for women would be lower, giving them a slight chance.

Seeing He Yan staring at the other’s face without speaking, Song Taotao grew even more anxious. She tugged at He Yan’s sleeve and said, “Why are you looking at her? What’s so good about her?”

The woman holding the golden cake rolls chuckled softly, her smile captivating.

“Ying Xiang,” someone spoke.

The maidservant named Ying Xiang immediately stopped smiling and bowed slightly toward the front. “Fourth Young Master.”

Fourth Young Master? Chu Zilan? He Yan turned around, her gaze falling on the person before her.

This was a young man dressed in a pale jade-colored robe with wide sleeves, wearing a jade crown. He was as elegant as an orchid and as handsome as an immortal. A faint smile graced his face as he nodded toward He Yan.

He Yan frowned. This person’s appearance seemed very familiar.

When he saw He Yan, he was also taken aback. After a moment, he smiled, as if understanding He Yan’s thoughts. He extended his hand, palm facing upward, and spoke softly, “Young brother, you dropped something.”

These words snapped He Yan back to reality. She remembered where she had seen this person before! Back when she was still in Shuojing, struggling to come up with the tuition for He Yunsheng’s studies, she had no choice but to gamble at Letong Manor. After being chased by the losers, she managed to defeat them all, only for someone to suddenly appear and tell her she had dropped some silver.

Such a handsome face was hard to forget once seen. Now, seeing him here so suddenly and in broad daylight, He Yan had not recognized him at first. Instead, he had recognized her first.

“You… Fourth Young Master Chu?” He Yan asked.

Chu Zilan nodded. “It’s me.”

For a moment, He Yan was speechless. What kind of luck did she have? Randomly climbing walls and fighting at night, yet she managed to run into the dream man of Great Wei’s young maidens. What kind of coincidence was this?

“I am Chu Zhao,” Chu Zilan said, smiling at He Yan. “Young brother and I are old acquaintances, but I still do not know your name. May I ask for your esteemed name?”

Such gentleness and politeness made He Yan understand why he could rival Xiao Jue. She quickly returned the courtesy and said, “You flatter me. I am He Yan. The ‘He’ of grass and trees, and the ‘Yan’ of peace and prosperity.”

Chu Zhao smiled. “A good name. However,” he looked around, puzzled, “why is Brother He here?”

“Me?” He Yan replied. “I am a new recruit of the Liangzhou Garrison, but I was injured a few days ago, so I have not been attending daily training at the martial arts field.”

“I see.”

At this moment, Song Taotao, who had been silent all along, finally caught on. She carefully tugged at He Yan’s hand, perhaps noticing how handsome Chu Zilan was. Her earlier hostility toward Ying Xiang instantly vanished, replaced by a hint of shyness. She whispered, “Brother He, who is this person? Do you know him?”

This was a difficult question to answer. She knew Chu Zhao, but not as well as Song Taotao imagined. It was just that seeing a familiar face at the Liangzhou Garrison had stirred a moment of instinctive excitement.

He Yan then said, “This is the Fourth Young Master of the Earl of Shijin’s residence. I once had a brief encounter with him when I was in Shuojing.”

Chu Zhao smiled and said, “We can be considered old friends.”

CONTENT END 119

chapters.title: Chapter 120. Drunkenness.
chapters.content:
While He Yan was speaking with Chu Zilan, she did not notice Xiao Jue and Lin Shuanghe standing behind a nearby tree.

Lin Shuanghe watched for a while, then remarked curiously, “It seems Sister He actually knows Chu Zilan? Then why did she say she did not know him when I asked her yesterday?”

“You asked her?”

“Yes, I even asked her whose side she would take if you and Chu Zilan ever came into conflict.” Lin Shuanghe fanned himself with a smile. “Want to know how she answered?”

Xiao Jue replied, “No.”

“Why are you like this?” Lin Shuanghe said. “I will tell you anyway. Sister He answered without hesitation that she did not know Chu Zilan, so of course, she would stand on your side. But,” he glanced at the two conversing in the distance, “she clearly knows him. Why would she say she does not?”

Xiao Jue scoffed. “Why would you believe the words of a deceiver?”

“A deceiver?” Lin Shuanghe looked at Xiao Jue. “What did she lie to you about? Could it be,” he thought of something and feigned a low gasp, “she’s in cahoots with Chu Zilan? Is she also one of Xu Jingfu’s people?”

Xiao Jue could not be bothered to respond.

Just then, the beautiful maid named Ying Xiang turned her head and happened to spot them. She immediately called out from afar, “General Xiao, Young Master Lin.”

Now, even if they wanted to hide, there was nowhere to go. Lin Shuanghe stepped forward and nodded politely. “Fourth Young Master Chu, Brother He.”

He Yan asked, “Are you two also out here to bask in the sun?”

“Just taking a casual stroll.” Lin Shuanghe fanned himself, his gaze shifting between He Yan and Chu Zhao as he probed, “Brother He and Fourth Young Master Chu knew each other before?”

He Yan replied, “We only met once. I only realized he was Fourth Young Master Chu when we met at the Liangzhou Garrison. I was quite surprised myself.”

“How did you meet? Care to share?” Lin Shuanghe pressed on relentlessly.

Chu Zhao stood there with a gentle smile, showing no intention of explaining. Xiao Jue’s gaze remained calm, yet it made He Yan feel a slight chill. Song Taotao, however, was very curious and urged, “Yes, yes, how did you two meet?”

“Well,” He Yan had no choice but to brace herself and explain, “Back in Shuojing, I went to Letong Manor one night to gamble, won a lot of silver, and was chased down. I accidentally ran into Fourth Young Master Chu. He picked up the silver I had dropped and returned it to me. At that time, I did not know his identity, so I thanked him hastily and left.”

“Letong Manor?” Song Taotao exclaimed in surprise. “Brother He, you gamble?”

“Did you not say your father was very strict with you, that you never left the house?” Lin Shuanghe could not help but ask.

He Yan looked up and met Xiao Jue’s half-smiling expression, which made her scalp tingle. She took a step back and said, “I was forced by circumstances back then… I only went once! I never went again!”

Both Lin Shuanghe and Xiao Jue knew she was a woman. For a woman to go gambling alone at night was quite shocking, and gambling itself was hardly a respectable activity. Having to admit this in front of such distinguished company was truly mortifying.

“I never imagined Brother He would later come to Liangzhou Garrison,” Chu Zhao said with a smile. “It seems fate brought us together. I still remember how skillfully you handled those thugs that night.”

“You are that skilled?” Lin Shuanghe asked He Yan.

He Yan replied with an evasive smile, “It was just luck.”

“Tonight’s victory banquet, I must share a few more cups with Brother He,” Chu Zhao said. “Only then will I not waste this fateful encounter.”

He Yan: “Th-thank you, Fourth Young Master Chu.”

She thought to herself, this Chu Zhao was far too approachable. As the son of the Earl of Shijin and now Xu Jingfu’s favored disciple, no matter how one looked at it, being so patient and gentle with an ordinary new recruit like her was truly rare. Regardless of whether he was good or bad, just in terms of being a good person, he was indeed impeccable.

“Ying Xiang,” Chu Zhao glanced at Song Taotao and smiled, “give the golden cake rolls to this young lady; I will not be able to finish them.”

Song Taotao was overwhelmed by the unexpected favor: “F-for me?”

“Yes,” he said gently. “If you like them very much, you can have the cook make them for you every day.”

“But Young Master,” Ying Xiang hesitated before speaking, “that cook was specially brought for you.”

“I am not particular about food,” Chu Zhao replied. “No need to make these every day.”

“Then…” Song Taotao hesitated for a moment, looking at him. “Thank you, Fourth Young Master Chu.”

“You are welcome.”

As He Yan watched, she thought of what Lin Shuanghe had said yesterday about Chu Zilan rising to first place in the Great Wei women’s dream lover rankings. No wonder he had surpassed others later on. With looks like that and such gentle, considerate treatment of women, it seemed he was the type that would be liked by all ages, young and old.

Ying Xiang handed the plate of golden cake rolls to Song Taotao. Chu Zhao looked at Xiao Jue: “General Xiao, where are you heading?”

“The martial arts field,” Xiao Jue raised the corner of his mouth. “Would Fourth Young Master Chu care to join?”

“I will pass,” Chu Zhao smiled. “I will just go back to my room and read for a while.”

Lin Shuanghe cupped his hands toward Chu Zhao: “Then we will see you tonight.” He then looked at He Yan: “What about you, Brother He?”

“Me?” He Yan did not dare stay with Chu Zhao too long either. This person was still Xu Jingfu’s student—who knew if he was friend or foe? So she said, “The weather is nice today. I plan to take advantage of the sun and walk around the courtyard more to recover.”

“That works too,” Lin Shuanghe advised. “Just do not make any big movements.”

He Yan nodded.

The group then parted ways.

Because Chu Zhao also lived nearby, He Yan did not dare go out casually, even though she really wanted to ask Chu Zhao about Shuojing. But judging by the atmosphere between Xiao Jue and Chu Zhao, now was not a good time for questions anyway.

She went to the courtyard, tried walking a bit without her stick, and stopped when she felt somewhat tired. Later, she returned to her room to sleep and read novels. In the blink of an eye, it was evening.

Cheng Lisu knocked on the door early: “Big Brother!”

He Yan went to open the door for him.

Cheng Lisu had changed into a brand new amber-colored robe, the hem still embroidered with a school of black-tailed koi. He was in high spirits and grabbed He Yan’s hand: “I was afraid you might be sleeping, so I did not come too early. How do you like my new robe?”

He Yan: “Can I ask you a question?”

“What?”

“Why do all your clothes have koi embroidered on them?”

Back in Liangzhou City, every robe Cheng Lisu gave her had koi embroidered on the hem. He Yan had wanted to ask him for a long time—was there some special meaning?

“You would not know this,” Cheng Lisu said, turning his back, “but to tell the story, my father fell in love with my mother at first sight back then. However, her family had already favored another match for her and disliked that my father was two years younger than my mother. So, my father bribed the cook in the estate to deliver a carp to the small kitchen where my mother’s meals were prepared. When the cook slaughtered the carp, he found a letter inside. My mother was moved by the letter and later persuaded my grandmother to marry my father.”

Cheng Lisu, who usually could not recall poetry or literature, now spoke fluently as if he had memorized it all: “A guest from afar, leaving me two carps; Hu’er then cooked the carp, within it a letter. Knelt reading the letter, what did the letter say? It began with enduring longing; it ended with ardent eating.” He said proudly, “My name comes from this.”

He Yan was stunned: “It’s actually that interesting?”

“Indeed,” Cheng Lisu turned back around, showing He Yan the carp embroidery on his clothes. “After that, most of my clothes and hairpins were shaped like carp. After all, the carp was the matchmaker for my parents. Wearing it is like wearing their love for me!”

At this moment, He Yan genuinely envied Cheng Lisu. She said, “Your parents are truly wonderful.”

“Of course,” Cheng Lisu replied, then looked at He Yan. “Brother, for tonight’s victory banquet, are you not going to wear something else?”

He Yan looked down at herself. “What’s wrong with what I am wearing? Everyone is dressed like this, right?”

She was still wearing the standard uniform of the Liangzhou Garrison recruits, but today she had deliberately chosen a festive red.

“But you are the great hero who defeated Rida Muzi. Wearing this is too ordinary.”

“I do not have any other clothes anyway,” He Yan said. “This is fine. Let’s go; the drillmasters might be getting impatient.”

Cheng Lisu shrugged and did not press further, casually closing the door for her as they headed together toward the wilderness at the foot of Baiyue Mountain.

Today was the victory banquet, celebrating the Liangzhou Garrison recruits’ success in annihilating Rida Muzi’s rebel forces. Tonight, there was no snow, but it felt colder than usual. A roaring bonfire burned in the wilderness, and the recruits sat on the ground, drinking and eating meat.

Although they were drinking and eating, compared to the Mid-Autumn Festival a while back, the atmosphere felt much more subdued. After all, they had just lost comrades, and the lingering fear of war had not yet faded. Celebrating a victory… felt somewhat forced.

The rewards had already been distributed to the drillmasters. Xiao Jue was very generous, distributing all the spoils of war among the soldiers and keeping none of the imperial rewards for himself. When Cheng Lisu reached the wilderness, he went to find Xiao Jue, while He Yan headed straight to Hong Shan’s side. She had not been to the martial arts field these days and had seen them much less often.

Xiao Mai called out when he saw her, “Brother He, you are here!”

He Yan sat down beside him.

“How are you?” Hong Shan handed her a piece of roasted rabbit meat. “Feeling better? I see you are not using a cane anymore. Can you walk now?”

He Yan took the rabbit meat. The rabbit was roasted until it sizzled with oil. In winter, most animals hibernate, making rabbits hard to catch. Just the smell alone made her mouth water. She took a bite and chewed as she spoke, “Not bad. In another two months, I will be able to fight alongside you all again.”

“Cut the crap,” Wang Ba said disdainfully. “Is it not always you hogging the spotlight? I heard the rewards from above gave you ten taels of silver alone.” He was extremely jealous. “You have struck it rich!”

“Brother He nearly lost his life. What’s ten taels of silver? He deserves even more,” Jiang Jiao interjected. “But I thought Brother He would get a promotion this time. I did not expect there to be none.”

Mentioning this made He Yan furious. Logically speaking, she had performed meritorious service and helped the Liangzhou Garrison. No matter what, she should not still be a lowly soldier. Even if she was not promoted, she should have been transferred to the Jiuqi Battalion. Even if not there, then at least to the Vanguard Battalion. But up to now, although her rewards were greater than those of ordinary recruits, a promotion? Not a trace of one.

Was it really this difficult to get promoted under Xiao Jue’s command?

“Stop talking, or Brother He will get upset again.” Huang Xiong noticed her displeasure and said, “You have already earned everyone’s respect in the Liangzhou Garrison. Even if not now, you will get promoted sooner or later. No need to rush.”

He Yan forced herself to say, “I am not in a hurry.”

But at night, she tossed and turned in bed, wishing she could rush into the next room, grab Xiao Jue, and demand an explanation.

Although it was called a victory banquet, Xiao Jue was not present, and the rewards had already been distributed in advance. So tonight was just a gathering of the recruits. The Liangzhou Garrison members sat near Baiyue Mountain, while the Southern Garrison Troops stayed by Wulu River, keeping to themselves without conflict.

Shitou poured He Yan a bowl of wine and said, “Drink up.”

He Yan stared at the wine in the bowl. “I am injured right now. I cannot drink this much.”

“That’s right, I almost forgot.” Hong Shan promptly took the wine bowl away. “Then do not drink wine. Just have water.”

He Yan replied, “Alright.”

After sitting for a while longer, she heard someone call from behind, “Brother He.”

He Yan turned around and was momentarily stunned—it was Chu Zhao.

Beside Chu Zhao was his stunningly beautiful maid, Ying Xiang. Such beautiful women were rare in the Liangzhou Garrison. For a moment, Hong Shan and the others were dumbstruck. Wang Ba muttered quietly, “This guy, how does he always have such good luck with women?”

He thought he was whispering, but everyone present heard him. Ying Xiang could not help but laugh, and Chu Zhao also smiled. “I promised Brother He earlier that I’d definitely come share a drink with you today.”

Ying Xiang added, “Before coming, our young master specially brought Chang’an Spring wine. Please join us for a drink, Young Master He.”

As soon as she finished speaking, Wang Ba audibly gulped.

He Yan: “…” She felt somewhat conflicted. If Xiao Jue found out she had gone drinking with Chu Zhao, would he think she was allied with him?

That would be a grave injustice.

As if sensing her hesitation, Chu Zhao smiled gently. “Just one cup. If it is inconvenient for Brother He, we can forget it.”

He Yan had always been more swayed by kindness than coercion. Seeing such an elegant young master extend a gentle invitation, knowing his boundaries and when to step back, she felt a pang of guilt. She was not some important figure who needed to be invited like this. It was just one cup of wine—consider it repaying the favor of that ingot of silver.

He Yan said, “It’s just one cup of wine. No inconvenience at all.”

“Then please follow this servant, Young Master He,” Ying Xiang said with a smile as she turned around.

He Yan had initially thought that when Chu Zhao mentioned drinking, it would be in the open field where the new recruits were stationed. To her surprise, he led her to his own quarters. She was not sure if Xiao Jue was settling personal scores under the guise of official duties, but Chu Zhao’s residence was far from luxurious—it was even less impressive than Cheng Lisu’s and only slightly better than the new recruits’ shared barracks. However, the courtyard was quite spacious, with a jug of wine and some dried fruits and pastries laid out on a stone bench.

“I was not sure what Young Master He might prefer, so I prepared some simple dishes,” Ying Xiang said apologetically. “If they do not suit your taste, please bear with me.”

“No need to be so polite; this is already more than enough,” He Yan replied, feeling both flattered and overwhelmed. In Liangzhou Garrison, she was merely a new recruit, and this was the first time she had been treated with such regard. Still, she could not help but wonder why Chu Zhao was being so kind to her. As a new recruit, there was no need for such courtesy.

As she pondered this, Ying Xiang picked up the white jade wine jug on the table and poured wine into two jade cups. “I heard from Young Master Lin that you have injuries, so strong liquor might not be suitable,” she said with a smile. “This Chang’an Spring is mild and sweet, so a little should not cause any trouble.”

He Yan smiled. “You have thought of everything, Miss Ying Xiang.”

Ying Xiang smiled softly, set down the wine jug, and retreated behind Chu Zhao.

“When we met in Shuojing last time, it was too rushed, and we did not have a chance to get to know each other properly,” Chu Zhao began with a gentle smile. “Since we have met again in Liangzhou, it seems fate has brought us together. Let’s toast to that.” He raised his cup and gestured toward He Yan in a toast.

Understanding his meaning, He Yan raised her cup as well, thinking to herself: Last time, during the Mid-Autumn Festival, I got drunk, fought with Xiao Jue, and even broke his qin. I must not repeat that mistake tonight. But this wine is not strong, and it will not go to my head like last time. Besides, I will only drink a little—it should be fine.

She tilted her head back and emptied the cup in one gulp.

He Yan froze.

Chu Zhao also froze.

After a moment, Chu Zhao chuckled. “Brother He, you truly are bold.”

He Yan: “…”

Drinking in one go had become a habit. Even though she had intended to take small sips, her hand moved instinctively. By the time she realized what she had done, she was filled with regret and wanted to scold herself: Why can I not control this hand?

But still… He Yan praised, “What fragrant wine!”

Ying Xiang could not help but laugh. “Chang’an Spring is not something you can drink every day. This is the last jug left in the Chu residence this year.”

“So precious?” He Yan exclaimed in surprise, pushing her cup back. She did not dare drink any more.

“Though the wine is precious, it cannot compare to you, Brother He,” Chu Zhao said with a smile, reaching for the wine jug and refilling He Yan’s empty cup. “If Chang’an Spring runs out, we can buy Eighteen Immortals. But if we lose a like-minded friend, it will not be so easy to find another.”

He Yan: “…”

She said, “Brother Chu, do you know you are ranked first in the dreams of Great Wei’s women?”

Chu Zhao was taken aback.

“I think we should add men to that list as well,” she continued. “Being so gentle and generous to men—any man who spends time with you is in danger too.”

The courtyard fell silent.

After a moment, Chu Zhao burst into hearty laughter, shaking his head. “Brother He, you truly are amusing.”

“I am just telling the truth,” He Yan replied earnestly.

“You flatter me, Brother He.” He waved his hand. “I dare not claim the title of first.”

Chang’an Spring smelled clear and crisp, not as rich and potent as Eighteen Immortals, yet its potency was not shallow. He Yan felt a bit light-headed. Seeing the gentle and refined smile on the man before her, she raised her wine cup and said to him, “Brother Chu deserves it. I toast to you!”

Another cup was drained in one go.

…

Meanwhile, Lin Shuanghe was searching everywhere for He Yan.

“Has anyone seen He Yan?” he asked.

The roasted meat on this side was all gone. Xiao Mai had just sneaked two pieces from the nearby fire pit. Hearing this, he turned around and said, “Are you looking for Brother He? Brother He was just taken away by the Fourth Young Master Chu from the capital.”

“Chu Zhao?” Lin Shuanghe asked curiously. “Why did he take Brother He away?”

“To drink, I suppose.” Xiao Mai scratched his head. “He said he wanted to treat Brother He to Chang’an Spring.”

Upon receiving this news, Lin Shuanghe hurried back without delay. Returning to Xiao Jue’s quarters, he found the door unlocked and pushed it open directly.

Xiao Jue was sitting at the table, cleaning his sword.

Yinqiu was no ordinary sword; it required daily cleaning and polishing to maintain its crystal-clear blade. Lin Shuanghe said, “Do you know where He Yan went?”

Xiao Jue ignored him.

“She was taken by Chu Zhao to drink!”

Xiao Jue glanced up. “So?”

“Are you not worried, Brother?” Lin Shuanghe slapped his fan on the table. “That’s Chu Zhao we are talking about!”

“Move aside,” Xiao Jue said impatiently. “You are blocking the light.”

Lin Shuanghe shifted to the side. “Stop polishing. On a public note, Chu Zhao is Xu Jingfu’s man. If he intends to recruit He Yan to their side, what will you do? I have heard He Yan’s skills are among the best in Liangzhou Garrison. If such talent falls into Xu Jingfu’s hands, it would be quite troublesome!”

Seeing that Xiao Jue’s expression remained unchanged, he circled to the other side. “On a private note, how can you let your girl go drinking with another man!”

At these words, Xiao Jue paused. He looked up and gave Lin Shuanghe a faint glance. “Who told you she’s mine?”

“Do not play dumb.” Lin Shuanghe made it clear he did not believe it. “If she is not yours, why would you let her live next door, with only a door between you, and even let her pick the lock? I never knew you could play like this. Quite the interest, huh?”

Xiao Jue: “… If you have nothing to do, get out and stop bothering me.”

“Xiao Huaijin, with this temper of yours, you are no match for Chu Zilan.”

As he spoke, a rustling sound came from the connecting door inside the room, as if a mouse were scurrying through the storage area. Both of them looked up and saw a silver wire poking through the keyhole of the door. The wire twisted and turned, accurately pushing the lock core inward.

With a click, the lock fell to the ground, and the door opened.

Lin Shuanghe clapped his hands. “Impressive skill!” He glanced at Xiao Jue again. “And you still say she is not yours!”

Xiao Jue fell silent for a moment, then stood up.

He Yan walked in from the doorway.

She walked slowly, her steps steady. Seeing Lin Shuanghe, she even greeted him first with a cupped-hand salute. “Brother Lin.”

Lin Shuanghe: “… Why are you not calling me Physician Lin anymore?”

But He Yan seemed not to notice him and walked straight to Xiao Jue.

Xiao Jue lowered his gaze, fixing it on He Yan.

The young man was dressed in the standard crimson uniform of the Liangzhou Garrison recruits, neat and proper, with not a single strand of hair out of place. He bowed respectfully to Xiao Jue.

At this, both Lin Shuanghe and Xiao Jue were stunned.

The window was left open, and the wind from outside blew in, gently rustling the scrolls on the table, bringing with it a cool breeze and a faint, elusive scent of wine. It was subtle yet distinct, carrying a sweet and refreshing aroma, reminiscent of a vibrant spring day in Chang’an, full of shimmering beauty.

Yet more captivating than spring was the look in her eyes.

Xiao Jue’s heart skipped a beat, struck by a sense of déjà vu. He vaguely recalled that on the night of the Mid-Autumn Festival, someone had looked at him with that same gaze.

“Have you been drinking?” he asked, instinctively pushing the Wanxiang qin further away as he spoke.

When this person was drunk, looking at her face alone, it was impossible to tell whether she was truly sober. But her actions would only leave people utterly bewildered.

Lin Shuanghe picked up his tea with a smile, intending to take a sip and enjoy the show.

He Yan raised her head and gave Xiao Jue a wide grin.

“I can recite ‘The Great Learning’ now, Father.”

Lin Shuanghe spat out his tea in one go.

CONTENT END 120

chapters.title: Chapter 121. Reward.
chapters.content:
“I’ve memorized it, Father.”

Xiao Jue stared at her in disbelief. “What did you call me?”

He Yan gazed at him, her eyes clear and earnest as she recited seriously, “The way of great learning lies in illuminating virtue, in renewing the people, and in resting in the highest good. Knowing where to rest leads to stability; with stability comes peace; with peace comes reflection; with reflection comes attainment… All things have their roots and branches; all affairs have their beginnings and ends… The extension of knowledge lies in the investigation of things… Cultivating the self is the foundation… To treat the important lightly and the unimportant heavily—such a thing has never been!”

Lin Shuanghe was first stunned, then gradually came to his senses. Pointing at He Yan, he asked Xiao Jue, “Is my Sister He… drunk?”

As soon as he finished speaking, He Yan suddenly rushed over, threw herself into Xiao Jue’s arms, and wrapped her arms around his waist, nearly causing him to stumble backward. She buried her face in his chest, rubbing against it, and said pitifully, “Father, I’ve memorized it. I’ve improved!”

The room fell into a deathly silence.

A few words alone could hardly describe the grim expression on Xiao Jue’s face at that moment.

Lin Shuanghe covered his face, his shoulders shaking as he laughed uncontrollably.

“Oh, Huaijin, I’ve seen people mistake you for their husband, but this is the first time I’ve seen someone mistake you for their father. How does it feel to be a father? This little daughter of yours is so well-behaved! She recites so well—quite talented!”

Seemingly encouraged by Lin Shuanghe’s praise of her “talent,” He Yan lifted her head from Xiao Jue’s chest and stared at him with sparkling eyes. “Father, I am now number one in Liangzhou Garrison.”

Xiao Jue grabbed her arm, trying to pry her hands from his waist. “Let go.”

“No!” He Yan’s grip was incredibly strong—perhaps from tossing stone locks all day—and Xiao Jue could not break free. She looked up at him and said, “Test me. I can answer anything.”

She was like a child who had won first place, wagging her tail and showing off at home.

Xiao Jue rubbed his forehead. “Let go first.”

“No.” She hugged Xiao Jue’s waist even tighter, pressing herself against him as if trying to merge with him. Xiao Jue desperately leaned back, trying to put distance between them and avoid physical contact, but it was futile.

As Xiao Jue tried to pry He Yan’s hands away, Lin Shuanghe interjected, “Ah, let me remind you, Sister He is still injured. If you force her, you might aggravate her wounds. It will take another half a year to heal—not ideal.”

Xiao Jue shot him a sharp glare. “Think of a way to get her off me.”

“Just let her hug you for a while,” Lin Shuanghe said, thoroughly enjoying the spectacle. “Maybe you look a lot like Sister He’s father, and she mistook you for him when she got drunk. She’s just a young girl who traveled all the way to Liangzhou and has not been home for so long. She must miss her father. Can you not give her a little,” he mimicked a hug, “warmth of home? Do not be so stingy—it’s not like you are losing anything.”

Before Xiao Jue could respond, the person in his arms buried her face in his chest again and began reciting in a muffled voice.
