He Yan felt puzzled. She was not that bad, was she? The way Chu Zhao laughed made it seem as if liking her was something absurd. After all, had not Song Taotao liked her back in the day?

“Brother He, rest assured.” Chu Zhao cleared his throat gently. “Physician Shen would absolutely never fall for you. There’s no need for you to worry or be troubled by this.”

He Yan: “… Why?”

“Because Physician Shen has liked General Xiao for many years. Her heart belongs only to him. How could anyone else catch her eye?”

He Yan was stunned.

After a long pause, she finally asked, “Physician Shen… likes the Commander?”

“Brother He, you do not know?” Chu Zhao was also surprised by her reaction. After thinking for a moment, he said, “Well, that makes sense. You are a new recruit in the Liangzhou Garrison, so you probably would not know about these things. But actually, all the colleagues in the court know that Physician Shen has liked General Xiao for many years.”

“The eldest daughter of the Censor’s household. If she were not truly, deeply in love with someone, why would she abandon her status as a young lady and, despite the long and arduous journey, come to such a harsh and desolate place just to serve as a lowly physician?” Chu Zhao smiled faintly. “It’s clear she’s utterly devoted to General Xiao.”

He Yan suddenly understood. In that moment, she suddenly remembered why she had felt such a sense of familiarity the first time she saw Shen Muxue. In fact, it was not the first time she had seen her. She had caught a glimpse of Shen Muxue once in her youth. Back then, Shen Muxue was even younger than she was now, but she had already blossomed into extraordinary beauty. On the day when the students of the Xianchang Academy went hunting in the mountains, the Emperor himself was present, along with many officials from the court. As the youngest daughter of Censor Shen, Shen Muxue had captured the attention of all the young men present at the time.

He Yan was also among those young men, gazing at the graceful girl wrapped in a rabbit-fur cloak, holding a hand warmer, as beautiful as a celestial maiden from the heavens, and filled with immense envy.

At that time, Shen Muxue had been watching Xiao Jue all along.

CONTENT END 163

chapters.title: Chapter 164. A Perfect Match.
chapters.content:
He Yan still remembered that during the hunting grounds back then, they were all young men in their teens. Suddenly encountering such a stunningly beautiful young lady, it was only natural that their gazes were drawn to her. It seemed it was Lin Shuanghe who remarked, “What a beautiful girl. If I say she deserves to be called the number one beauty of Shuojing City, no one would disagree, right?”

“No objections here!”

“Who would have thought that Censor Shen, with his foul temper, would have such a breathtakingly beautiful daughter?”

Censor Shen was upright and sharp-tongued, daring to speak bluntly even before Emperor Wenxuan. He was also extremely strict in his daily conduct. If anyone in the court made even the slightest mistake, he would submit one or two memorials of impeachment against them. However, the previous emperor had praised Censor Shen for embodying the noble spirit of Great Wei, and the current Empress Dowager was particularly fond of him. His position was solid and unshakable, so his colleagues in the court could only keep a respectful distance. The more his colleagues isolated Censor Shen, the more Emperor Wenxuan felt that Censor Shen was pitifully upright, a paragon of integrity among officials, and thus treated him with exceptional leniency.

With such a father, whose temper was as stubborn as a rock, his daughter was born with an otherworldly beauty. When the term “difficult to approach” was applied to an old man, it meant he was eccentric and harsh. But when applied to a graceful young lady, it meant she was aloof and ethereal, untouched by worldly affairs.

He Yan also remembered that although Shen Muxue was a girl and quite young at the time, when the hunt ended and the game was tallied, as Xiao Jue stepped forward to receive the emperor’s commendation, his cloak fell to the ground. It should have been picked up by his attendant or servant, but that fairy-like Physician Shen walked up herself, picked up the cloak, and handed it to Xiao Jue, who was still on horseback.

At that moment, all the young men were somewhat astonished. Someone remarked sourly, “It’s over, it is over. We’ve been chattering away excitedly here, but this girl has her eyes set on Brother Huaijin.”

“Why is Brother Huaijin so popular with the ladies? Could he not leave a little face for the rest of us?”

Lin Shuanghe sighed, fanning himself. “That’s naturally because this Physician Shen is also someone who judges by appearances.”

He Yan followed the gazes of the others and looked over. She saw the arrogant and dashing young man on horseback and the reserved, graceful girl standing below. In terms of appearance alone, they were enough to be called a celestial couple, a perfect match.

She silently lowered her head, looking at her empty hands that had caught no game, and sighed inwardly. Outstanding people should be with other outstanding people. All she could do, it seemed, was stand far away and watch others shine with confidence and vigor.

“Brother He?” Chu Zhao’s voice pulled He Yan’s thoughts back.

He Yan snapped back to reality and asked, “But if Physician Shen has traveled all the way to Liangzhou, would Censor Shen agree?”

Censor Shen had only one son and one daughter. Compared to his strictness toward his eldest son, he was exceptionally doting toward his younger daughter. Shen Muxue appeared obedient and proper. Although He Yan did not think it was an unforgivable sin for a woman to go to the military camp, in the eyes of most people, it was probably considered deviant. Moreover, as a censor, how could Censor Shen allow his daughter to act so recklessly?

“Physician Shen was determined to leave, and Censor Shen could not stop her. Besides,” Chu Zhao smiled, “to tell the truth, when General Xiao was alive, he was on close terms with the Shen family. Censor Shen and General Xiao were originally good friends. After the Xiao family’s incident, Censor Shen also helped out a great deal. General Xiao is young and accomplished. On one hand, Censor Shen trusts him, and on the other…” He paused. “He probably harbors some intention of forming a marriage alliance with the Xiao family.”

He Yan’s heart skipped a beat, and she instinctively retorted, “How could that be?”

Chu Zhao looked at her, seemingly puzzled by her reaction. “Why not?”

“… The Commander usually keeps his distance from women,” He Yan said, feigning nonchalance. “His mind is only on military affairs. From what I’ve seen, he does not interact much with Shen Muxue either.”

Xiao Jue was cold and aloof toward everyone, and he never showed Shen Muxue any special treatment.

“A-He, you are a girl,” Chu Zhao chuckled. “You do not understand a man’s heart. If there were such an outstanding and gentle girl, saying nothing but silently accompanying him day after day, following him through battles north and south, even someone with a heart of stone would be moved. ‘Moved’ turns into ‘pity,’ and ‘pity’ becomes ‘affection.’ Since General Xiao has not sent her away, it must be because he harbors pity for her.”

He Yan pursed her lips and said nothing, feeling that Chu Zhao’s words were rather unpleasant to hear.

“If it were you, would pity also turn into affection?” He Yan asked.

Chu Zhao was taken aback for a moment, then shook his head. “No.”

“Then why would it not?”

Chu Zhao looked at her, a flicker of amusement in his eyes. “I do not like gentle girls.”

“I prefer lively and spirited ones.”

He Yan glanced at him but said nothing, thinking to herself that it was hard to imagine someone as mild-mannered and quiet as Chu Zhao liking lively and spirited girls.

The room was just ahead. Chu Zhao smiled and said, “I will leave you here. Rest early tonight. You have daily training tomorrow.”

He Yan nodded, thanked him, and entered the room.

The connecting door was closed today, and she had no idea whether Xiao Jue was asleep on the other side. On any other day, He Yan might have knocked on the door or picked the lock to chat for a bit, but today she was not in the mood. After washing up, she lay down on the bed, staring at the ceiling, her thoughts drifting back to what Chu Zhao had said earlier. She could not help but feel unsettled.

Xiao Jue and Shen Muxue?

She had not thought much of it before, but after hearing Chu Zhao’s words tonight, she realized there were things she had overlooked. Why was Shen Muxue the only female physician’s aide in Liangzhou Garrison? She had once heard Shen Han call her “Physician Shen.” The instructors not only felt grateful toward Shen Muxue but even held a certain respect for her. So that was why.

The daughter of Censor Shen, the son of General Xiao—their families were equally distinguished, their appearances equally outstanding, and even their fathers were close friends.

He Yan turned over, facing the wall, and thought with a sour heart, “They really are a perfect match.”

…

The next day, it was time for daily training again.

With the experience from the first day, the second day felt much more familiar. The daily training in the Southern Garrison Troops did not include paired combat drills, so without any sparring, everything was peaceful. Moreover, the Southern Garrison Troops mostly practiced military formations, which He Yan was already familiar with. She kept up with every change in the formations without ever falling behind, which even surprised Tian Lang.

“What do you think?” Shen Han asked Tian Lang as he watched He Yan in the formation. “This kid is not bad, right?” Although He Yan was now part of the Southern Garrison Troops, she had come from Liangzhou Garrison, so Shen Han was still quite concerned about her. Besides, this kid had a close relationship with Xiao Jue, and Shen Han believed he should keep an eye on her.

Tian Lang replied, “He has good potential.”

Shen Han found it amusing to recall that when He Yan first arrived at Liangzhou Garrison, Xiao Jue had personally concluded that her aptitude was far too poor. At the time, none of the instructors had held any high hopes for He Yan, believing she would inevitably be driven off to become a cook. Yet now, it was He Yan who had gone the furthest. Truly, who could predict the twists and turns of the battlefield?

The other instructors also gathered around. While the new recruits of Liangzhou Garrison were resting, the Southern Garrison Troops had far less downtime, so they took the opportunity to see how He Yan was adapting.

“Did not disgrace our Liangzhou Garrison!” Liang Ping boasted, though he tried to sound modest. “In the future, we will have to trouble Deputy Commander Tian to teach this lad a thing or two! Do not worry about our pride—discipline him as needed!”

Tian Lang: “…”

Ma Damei chuckled. “Deputy Commander Tian, this young man learns quickly—and this is not just us bragging about Liangzhou Garrison. If you teach him more, he will surely surprise you often in the future.”

Tian Lang was speechless. To him, He Yan was merely a new recruit with decent aptitude who happened to have earned Xiao Jue’s trust. In terms of skill and talent, there were far more outstanding individuals in the Southern Garrison Troops, not to mention the Jiuqi Battalion. It was just that Liangzhou Garrison was remote, and having finally produced someone like this, they treated him like a treasure—a sign of their limited perspective.

As they spoke, a woman in a pale blue dress approached from a distance. Liangzhou Garrison had only one woman, and everyone greeted her: “Physician Shen.”

Shen Muxue walked over.

She set down the basket in her hands and said, “I gathered some medicinal herbs and have already washed and dried them. Could the instructors have someone boil these herbs into a medicinal broth? With the transition from spring to summer, if each soldier drinks a spoonful, it can help ward off the cold.”

Shen Han quickly thanked her. “We appreciate your hard work, Physician Shen.” He then turned to instruct someone to take the basket away and brew the medicine immediately.

Shen Muxue was in no hurry to leave. Instead, she looked toward the soldiers training on the martial arts field, her gaze settling on the slender figure among the ranks.

He Yan blended into the crowd, her stature unremarkable, yet she somehow remained impossible to overlook. Over the years, she had followed Xiao Jue to various places and met many people. Countless new recruits had come and gone, but only this one left a lasting impression. Like a nimble breeze, she stood apart from everyone around her.

That jar of hand balm… It was just an ordinary jar of balm. She rarely desired anything, and even when she expressed a wish to Xiao Jue, it would have been a simple gesture. Yet Xiao Jue had stopped her, and not long after, she found it in He Yan’s possession.

Had Xiao Jue refused her because of He Yan?

It was natural to show more care for a capable young man who might become a trusted confidant in the future. Shen Muxue understood this, but even with his trusted aides like Chi Wu and Fei Nu, while Xiao Jue trusted them, he would never go to such lengths—it was almost as if… as if he were treating a young lady. Reflecting on this, Shen Muxue felt that Xiao Jue’s treatment of He Yan was excessively kind. It was Cheng Lisu’s room, yet after Cheng Lisu left, He Yan had not moved out. For a new recruit to live next door to the Right Army Commander was rather unusual. Moreover, Xiao Jue did not maintain the same aloof distance with He Yan as he did with others, even tacitly allowing many of her unconventional actions.

It was this very indulgence that made Shen Muxue uneasy.

Perhaps it was that women’s thoughts were always particularly delicate, and their intuition exceptionally accurate. This time, after Xiao Jue and He Yan returned, Shen Muxue felt even more that something was amiss.

She did not want to leave just yet, wishing to stay a moment longer at the martial arts field, so she said, “I prepared some medicine in advance; the instructors may drink it first. The medicine buckets are placed not far away. I must trouble the instructors to find a young man to accompany me to fetch them.”

Shen Han said, “How could we trouble Physician Shen like this? I will accompany you.” With that, he informed the others and followed Shen Muxue into the distance.

Watching Shen Muxue’s departing figure, Liang Ping sighed, “Physician Shen truly has a Bodhisattva’s heart, and she is so beautiful. How can there be such a flawless woman in this world? If I could marry her, it would be worth dying for in this lifetime.”

“You think quite beautifully,” another instructor on the side mocked him upon hearing this. “How could someone like you, an ordinary mortal, dare to harbor such thoughts about Physician Shen? You must know that there are so many talented young men in the court, and she does not even spare them a glance. How could she possibly take a liking to a mere instructor like you?”

“What’s wrong with being an instructor?” Liang Ping retorted indignantly. “Since Physician Shen is willing to lower herself to come to a harsh and bitter place like Liangzhou, does not look down on us rough folk, and even brews medicine for everyone, it shows she is someone who does not despise the poor or fawn over the rich but is noble-minded and kind-hearted. Such a person must judge others solely by their character,” he muttered quietly. “My character is excellent; what if… just maybe?”

Ma Damei could not bear to listen any longer. “She lowered herself, but not for you.”

“Exactly, Old Liang. She did it for General Xiao. What do you have to compare with General Xiao? Are you as handsome as he? Are you as skilled in martial arts? Or in family background, talent, demeanor, or strategy—you fall short in every aspect, yet you dare to boast shamelessly here. If I were Physician Shen and heard such insolence from you, I’d have my servants come out and beat you to death with a stick, lest you tarnish her reputation.”

Liang Ping: “… Are you still my brothers?”

As they were talking, a voice suddenly called out from the side: “Instructors!”

Everyone looked over. The Southern Garrison Troops were now on a break, and He Yan, spotting the instructors standing on the high platform, came over to greet them. Perhaps because she was no longer considered part of the Liangzhou Garrison and her superior was now Tian Lang, her interactions with the former instructors had become more like those between friends. She leaped onto the platform, walked into the midst of the group, greeted each of them one by one, and asked with a smile, “What were you all talking about just now? It seemed so lively.”

“We were saying there’s a toad among us, dreaming of eating swan meat,” one instructor replied with a grin.

He Yan asked curiously, “What does that mean?”

“We were talking about Physician Shen,” Ma Damei explained with a smile. “We said Physician Shen is of noble status, pure in character, and beloved by all.”

He Yan was taken aback, and to make matters worse, someone with no sense of self-preservation leaned in close and whispered mysteriously to her, “Brother He, do you know what background Physician Shen comes from?”

If this had been before last night, He Yan might have been quite surprised. But having already learned Shen Muxue’s identity from Chu Zhao, it no longer seemed strange. That person was not one to keep quiet either; without waiting for He Yan to speak, he said, “Physician Shen is now the young lady of the Censor’s household! Someone of such noble status—if not for General Xiao, why would she travel thousands of li like this? If I had such a beauty treating me this way, I would absolutely be good to her and only her for the rest of my life!”

He Yan thought to herself, had she recently been constantly clashing with the name Shen Muxue? One after another, why must they all line up to stab her in the heart?

“None of what you are saying is reliable,” Liang Ping stubbornly insisted, unwilling to admit defeat. “If General Xiao truly liked Physician Shen, why has he not said anything until now? I am a man, I understand best. If a man likes a woman, he cannot possibly hide it. Those who can hide it are not that fond. The world is vast; why should Physician Shen hang herself on one tree? She’d be better off opening her eyes and looking around—maybe fate is right beside her.”

“Liang Ping, you are really sick, and seriously ill at that. I think Physician Shen should send you two doses of medicine to check your eyes. What’s wrong with your brain? How can you say such shameless things?”

Amid the noisy chatter, Tian Lang quietly shifted a step to the side. He had no intention of joining this mess of recklessly discussing their superiors. If caught, he’d really be in deep trouble.

He Yan also wanted to slip away, not wanting to listen to these heart-stabbing words. But the others would not let her off. One instructor patted her shoulder and said, “Brother He, why are you not saying anything? You are one of us too. Tell us, are Physician Shen and General Xiao not a match made in heaven? Old Shen is overestimating himself, is he not?”

He Yan: “…”

Everyone looked at her eagerly, as if her comment was of utmost importance.

Bracing herself, He Yan forced a smile despite the overwhelming reluctance in her heart. “… Yes, Physician Shen is a renowned beauty, radiant as spring blossoms. General Xiao is noble and handsome, with an imposing presence. They truly are a match made in heaven.”

As soon as the words left her mouth, bitterness threatened to overflow. She thought to herself, what had she done to deserve this? Listening to others stab her heart was bad enough, but now she had to stab herself, too.

“What about their status? Is that not also well-matched?”

He Yan: “…Yes, the Right Army Commander and the Censor’s daughter are people from the same world. It has nothing to do with any of us.”

“Brother He, you are quite trusted by the Commander now. Maybe when the Commander gets married, he will even invite you to the ceremony. Such a congratulatory event; should you not start saving up now to prepare a wedding gift?”

He Yan mentally etched the speaker’s face firmly in her mind, gritting her teeth inwardly while maintaining a calm and composed expression on the outside. “Of course, for such a congratulatory event, a grand gift is a must.”

Everyone burst into laughter and actually began brainstorming what He Yan should give when Xiao Jue and Shen Muxue got married. Not a single person noticed He Yan’s stiff expression.

“Are you all very idle?” A cold voice sounded from behind.

Everyone turned to look. Unnoticed, Xiao Jue had arrived, followed by Shen Muxue and Shen Han carrying a medicine bucket.

Knowing they had been caught red-handed gossiping about their superior’s private affairs in secret, the group was so terrified they fell silent, not daring to utter a word. They still clung to a sliver of hope—Xiao Jue probably had not heard much. Otherwise, given his temperament, he would have stopped them as soon as he heard. Since he spoke up only now, he must have just arrived.

Xiao Jue stepped forward. The dark blue brocade robe accentuated his jade-like complexion and moon-like grace, yet his voice was cold. Though his words were directed at everyone, his eyes were fixed on He Yan, sharp and profound as if concealing blades.

“With so much free time to gossip here, I take it your daily training is going exceptionally well.”

The instructors immediately turned into quails, not one daring to speak. Tian Lang felt greatly relieved—fortunately, he had been perceptive enough to distance himself early from this ragtag group. See? They had been caught. Instantly, he stood even straighter with pride, making himself appear uniquely upright compared to the others.

Shen Han inwardly groaned. If only he had sent Liang Ping to fetch the medicine barrels with Shen Muxue. When he and Shen Muxue returned, they had run into Xiao Jue heading toward the martial arts field. The three of them arrived together, only to witness everyone asking He Yan whether Xiao Jue and Shen Muxue were a good match.

Whoever asked that question must have had ulterior motives! How could they put He Yan in such a position? Was that not like stabbing someone in the heart? Before he could even identify the genius who had asked, he heard He Yan answer without hesitation.

“… Yes, Physician Shen is a renowned beauty, radiant as spring blossoms. General Xiao is noble and handsome, a man of exceptional character. They are truly a match made in heaven.”

Shen Han could immediately feel the chilling aura emanating from the person beside him. Stealing a cautious glance at Xiao Jue, his expression was as unpleasant as if his wife had been stolen.

Shen Han inwardly beat his chest in frustration. Why was it always him stumbling upon such awkward situations? He had lived an honest and cautious life, never doing anything wrong—why was it so difficult?

He Yan looked at Xiao Jue. The young commander stared back expressionlessly, a trace of mockery curling at the corner of his lips. “As a new recruit, you are mingling with instructors. Since you have so much energy, it seems your daily training is not enough.”

He turned to Tian Lang and said calmly, “He Yan’s daily training can be doubled.”

Tian Lang: “… Yes.”

Xiao Jue raised an eyebrow coldly. “Not going yet?”

He Yan glanced at him. “Yes.” She turned and jumped off the platform, walking back into the ranks.

She could sense that Xiao Jue was displeased with her. But… was she not the one who should be angrier? He Yan rejoined the ranks, picked up her spear again, and her gaze fell on the figure on the platform. Beside him stood Shen Muxue, a jade-like beauty—a perfect match made in heaven.

He Yan lowered her head.

The instructors present were punished one by one, leaving dejectedly. Before departing, they were warned: anyone in the Liangzhou Garrison who dared to spout nonsense again would be packing their bags and returning home.

Tian Lang had long since slipped away under the pretext of needing to drill the troops. On the martial arts field, only Shen Han and Shen Muxue remained, the former wishing he could turn himself into a piece of furniture.

Shen Muxue stood behind Xiao Jue, gazing at his tall, straight figure, a wave of indescribable bitterness welling up in her heart.

Earlier, when she and Shen Han arrived, hearing people discussing her and Xiao Jue together, aside from embarrassment and annoyance, she had actually felt joy.

She enjoyed hearing these things and liked having her name linked with Xiao Jue’s. It was as if only in this way could it illustrate the relationship between her and Xiao Jue, and also hint that she was a very special one to him. So when she heard He Yan say that, Shen Muxue was very pleased.

But when she looked up and saw the instant chill in Xiao Jue’s eyes, she froze.

She would not dare claim to understand Xiao Jue completely, but she still had a good grasp of this man’s joys and sorrows. He did not like hearing people say such things; unlike her own secret delight, Xiao Jue was even somewhat angry.

Why would someone feel angry upon hearing such a thing? There was only one reason: the person who heard it simply did not like her.

Xiao Jue did not like her.

Shen Muxue’s expression turned somber, and within that somberness, there was also a hint of confusion. If he did not like hearing it, he could have simply ignored it, but such anger was still somewhat unexpected. Xiao Jue was someone who rarely showed his emotions on his face; when it came to many things, he mostly did not care.

But he cared deeply this time. Why?

CONTENT END 164

chapters.title: Chapter 165. Not Allowed to Go.
chapters.content:
The sky gradually darkened.

The medicinal brews prepared for the drillmasters had all been taken and consumed by them. Since Lin Shuanghe arrived at Liangzhou Garrison, Xiao Jue’s decoctions had been handled by Lin Shuanghe, leaving Shen Muxue without even a conversational opening. Standing there, Shen Muxue watched as Xiao Jue focused intently on the daily training drills of the Southern Garrison Troops, showing no intention of speaking with her. As time passed, an awkwardness naturally settled in.

After all, she was the delicate and noble young lady of the Censor’s household, her deeply ingrained pride formidable. She could abandon everything to share hardships with Xiao Jue, forsaking the life of a pampered official’s daughter to serve as a medical attendant in such a harsh and bitter land. Yet she could not bring herself to express her feelings to Xiao Jue as openly and directly as girls from ordinary families, or even servants and maids.

Shen Muxue had always hoped that as long as she stayed by Xiao Jue’s side, he would eventually recognize her virtues and take the initiative to tell her that they were the most perfectly matched pair in the world. This was her reserve, and she had always felt secure, for over the years, many stunning beauties had thrown themselves at Xiao Jue, yet he had never shown the slightest interest. Xiao Jue simply kept women at a distance.

But now, Shen Muxue was perplexed. Certain things gave her a foreboding sense: what if, before she could make Xiao Jue see her worth, he had already fallen in love with someone else?

Shen Muxue could not bear to imagine such a scene.

Picking up the empty bamboo basket, she turned to leave without bidding farewell to Xiao Jue. When Xiao Jue was drilling troops, he disliked being disturbed—over the years, she had come to understand his preferences thoroughly.

“Physician Shen,” someone called out to her.

Shen Muxue looked up to see a man in wide sleeves and a long robe smiling and pointing ahead. “If you keep walking with your head down like that, you will bump into the stone up ahead.”

Not far away stood a massive boulder. The new recruits of Liangzhou Garrison often liked to sharpen their blades or hack at it recklessly, leaving its surface pitted with scars and carved with all sorts of crude insults. Distracted, she had failed to notice such a large stone. Had Chu Zhao not warned her, she would have walked straight into it.

Shen Muxue halted and gave a slight bow to Chu Zhao. “Fourth Young Master Chu.”

She knew that Xiao Jue and Chu Zhao held opposing stances, as Chu Zhao was, after all, Minister Xu’s prized disciple. Yet Chu Zhao was handsome and gentle in temperament, making it difficult for ordinary women to harbor ill feelings toward him. Shen Muxue was no exception; whenever they met, she never neglected proper etiquette.

“Physician Shen seems preoccupied,” Chu Zhao said with a faint smile. “Could it be that you are troubled over General Xiao?”

Shen Muxue was startled, momentarily flustered by the sense that her innermost thoughts had been exposed. However, she quickly composed herself and replied softly, “Not at all. I was merely pondering the medical principles from the texts I read today. Fourth Young Master Chu is overthinking.”

Chu Zhao nodded and was about to continue on his way. As they passed each other, Shen Muxue felt a sudden impulse and asked, “Fourth Young Master Chu seems to be on good terms with a recruit named He Yan in Liangzhou Garrison?”

Shen Muxue had seen Chu Zhao speaking with He Yan on several occasions. Although Chu Zhao was usually approachable and never put on airs as an official’s son, he was by no means an enthusiastic or talkative person. At Liangzhou Garrison, aside from conversing with that excessively beautiful maidservant, he had little interaction with others. Yet with He Yan, his demeanor was notably warm and friendly.

“Brother He?” Chu Zhao paused. “Brother He is my good friend from Liangzhou Garrison. Does Physician Shen have something to ask of him?”

His straightforward acknowledgment left Shen Muxue momentarily at a loss for what to ask next. After a moment, she looked at Chu Zhao and said, “When the Wutu people attacked Jiyang, I heard that Fourth Young Master Chu was also there, staying at the residence of the Central Cavalry Officer along with the Commander and the others. Since Fourth Young Master Chu is also a close friend of He Yan, you must know quite a bit about him.”

Chu Zhao listened quietly as she spoke.

Shen Muxue hesitated before asking, “How is the relationship between the Commander and He Yan? Do they get along well?”

“Physician Shen, your question is somewhat odd.” Chu Zhao’s gaze swept over the woman before him. Shen Muxue nervously twisted the hem of her skirt. Chu Zhao smiled, “Brother He is highly skilled and straightforward in temperament, earning General Xiao’s trust. Physician Shen should know better than anyone that General Xiao is by no means an easy person to approach. However, Brother He is no ordinary man; he seems to have effortlessly opened General Xiao’s heart.”

“Rather than being master and subordinate, I believe the relationship between General Xiao and Brother He is more like that of friends.”

“Friends?” Shen Muxue’s voice sharpened slightly for an instant. She frowned. “The Right Army Commander and a new recruit—their statuses are so different. How could they be friends?”

Chu Zhao laughed. “Physician Shen, you are mistaken. Making friends should always follow the heart and nature. Age, status, and position are unimportant. How can there be distinctions of high and low, noble and humble, among friends? General Xiao has always treated Brother He very well. In Jiyang, the two of them shared a room and ate at the same table. General Xiao even arranged clothing and attire for Brother He. To call them merely superior and subordinate would be far too forced.”

Shen Muxue listened, her heart secretly trembling.

Xiao Jue was fastidious and solitary. Sharing a meal at the same table was already his limit. Sharing a room? She could hardly imagine it. And arranging attire for He Yan—when had he ever cared about such trivial details for others?

Chu Zhao stared into Shen Muxue’s eyes. “What is Physician Shen worried about?”

Meeting his thoughtful gaze, Shen Muxue could not help but take a step back, instinctively shaking her head in denial. “Nothing.”

“Physician Shen, as a woman, you traveled all the way from Shuojing to Liangzhou. You must be determined, brave, and forthright. Why do you falter in this matter?”

Shen Muxue pressed her lips together and remained silent.

“What Physician Shen fears, I can guess a little. Brother He is my friend, so I cannot say too much. However, I also admire Physician Shen’s sincerity. So… if Physician Shen truly cannot let go, why not seek the truth yourself? Sometimes,” he said calmly, “one should trust their intuition, especially… a woman.”

Shen Muxue looked up. The man before her still wore a gentle smile, his gaze warm and concerned, yet it made her feel an involuntary chill spreading over her body.

“I… do not understand what Fourth Young Master Chu means,” she said as she frowned, tightened her grip on the basket in her hand, and quickly walked past Chu Zhao. “I must return to prepare the medicinal herbs. Farewell, Fourth Young Master Chu.”

Shen Muxue hurried away, her retreating figure looking rather flustered. Chu Zhao watched her back, the smile on his face fading slightly. After a moment, he murmured to himself, “This is getting more and more interesting.”

“Shen Muxue,” he whispered, “Xiao Huaijin, which one will you choose?”

…

The daily training for the new recruits in the martial arts field had ended.

As Lin Shuanghe passed by the martial arts field, he happened to see Xiao Jue dismissing the Southern Garrison Troops. He went over to greet him, intending to return together for a meal.

“Huaijin, have you not been pushing my Sister He too hard in training these past few days? I have not seen her in a long time. I must remind you, she still has injuries. Though not too serious, girls are not like men—they need more rest. You should be more considerate.”

Xiao Jue replied coldly, “Mind your own business.”

“How can this be called meddling? Sister He is my friend, and yours too. Friends should help each other.”

“Worry about yourself first.”

Lin Shuanghe fanned himself with his folding fan, keenly sensing that Xiao Jue was in a rather bad mood today. Although this man rarely showed his emotions, whether good or bad, on his face… after all, they had been friends for many years, and some subtle hints could still be detected.

Just as he was about to ask, he looked up and saw someone else walking ahead in the distance. Within Liangzhou Garrison, aside from new recruits and instructors, those not wearing the standard uniform always stood out. Lin Shuanghe called out, “Fourth Young Master Chu?”

Chu Zhao turned around and, seeing Xiao Jue and Lin Shuanghe, nodded. “General Xiao, Young Master Lin.”

“It’s so late; what brings Fourth Young Master Chu here?” Lin Shuanghe asked.

“I just took a walk by the Wulu River and am heading back now.”

The weather was gradually warming, carrying the heat of early summer. The Wulu River had lost its wintry chill and was now cool and pleasant. A walk by the river at night was indeed comfortable.

Xiao Jue remained frosty and could not be bothered to acknowledge Chu Zhao. Lin Shuanghe, however, was naturally sociable and could not bear to let the atmosphere become so stiff. Yet, he and Chu Zhao had never interacted much, so he had to make small talk. He asked Chu Zhao, “What is that tied to your waist, Fourth Young Master Chu?”

Chu Zhao followed his gaze and smiled. “It’s just a stone.”

Lin Shuanghe was somewhat curious. As the Fourth Young Master of the Chu family and Xu Jingfu’s prized disciple, Chu Zhao’s attire, while not overly extravagant, was still refined. Lin Shuanghe had assumed the item at his waist was a piece of jade, never expecting it to be a stone. Was the Chu family on the verge of collapse? So destitute?

As if noticing Lin Shuanghe’s surprise, Chu Zhao smiled, untied the stone from his waist, and handed it to him.

Lin Shuanghe took a look. It was a flat, ordinary stone, naturally shaped like a horse, with traces of carving at the tail. The head and body of the horse had also been chiseled. If it were made of jade, it might have been considered interesting and lively, but as a stone, it more resembled a toy for children, with nothing particularly remarkable about it.

It truly was just a stone.

“Why would Fourth Young Master Chu think to carry a stone on his person?” Lin Shuanghe handed the stone back to him, clearing his throat twice. “This stone hardly matches your status.”

“The sentiment of a friend makes even a stone priceless,” Chu Zhao replied earnestly.

Upon hearing these words, Lin Shuanghe immediately felt a mischievous urge and smiled as he looked at Chu Zhao. “Does Fourth Young Master Chu mean this was a gift from a sweetheart?” His impression of Chu Zhao had greatly changed, knowing that Chu Zhao was someone Xu Pingting had her eye on. No matter how capable Chu Zhao was, he would not dare openly defy Minister Xu, who doted on his precious daughter above all else. Xu Pingting, with her lofty standards, would certainly not give Chu Zhao a mere stone. The girl who could give such a gift was likely from an ordinary family. Yet Chu Zhao dared to openly wear something given by a woman other than Xu Pingting, unafraid of being discovered by the Xu father and daughter, which would surely bring him trouble.

How could one not admire such boldness?

Chu Zhao was taken aback for a moment, then shook his head with a smile. “It’s not from a sweetheart. It is from Brother He.”

At these words, the surroundings fell silent.

Xiao Jue’s gaze settled on Chu Zhao’s face, while Lin Shuanghe could not help but ask eagerly, “You said it was given by Brother… He?”

“Sort of,” Chu Zhao replied. “The stone was originally carved and completed by her.”

Lin Shuanghe was utterly shocked.

Despite all precautions, He Yan had still fallen into it! Even giving a stone as a gift—such an act clearly showed deep affection. But it was not entirely her fault. At an age when feelings first blossom, who could resist the gentle and charming advances of a handsome young master?

If it were anyone else, it might not matter, but Lin Shuanghe believed Chu Zilan was far from a suitable match. Not to mention the messy affairs in Chu Linfeng’s household, just dealing with Xu Pingting alone would be difficult. He Yan, after all, had no notable background or connections. If Xu Pingting wanted to find a reason to target He Yan, it would be as easy as turning over her hand. If Chu Zhao truly cared for He Yan, the best course of action would be to keep his distance respectfully. Yet by being so open and unguarded, was he not making He Yan a living target, waiting for Xu Pingting to come and cause trouble?

Moreover, Chu Zhao knew He Yan’s true identity as a woman.

For a moment, even the usually “friendly” Lin Shuanghe regarded Chu Zhao with a hint of hostility.

Chu Zhao, perceptive as ever, noticed the sudden hostility in Lin Shuanghe’s eyes but remained unfazed. He then turned to look at Xiao Jue. The young master’s dark blue brocade robe took on a cool, desolate hue under the night sky. His figure was tall and upright, his eyes dark and unfathomable as he gazed calmly at Chu Zhao.

There seemed to be a sharp edge to his gaze.

With a smile, Chu Zhao cupped his hands in a salute. “My room is just ahead, so I will not disturb General Xiao and Young Master Lin any further. Until tomorrow.” With that, he turned and walked in another direction.

“This Chu Zilan seems rather unwelcoming,” Lin Shuanghe murmured, watching his retreating figure.

It seemed he was targeting He Yan.

…

The lamp in the room was lit once more.

Xiao Jue changed out of his clothes and sat down at the table. During the day, he had observed the training of new recruits at the martial arts field, and at night, he still had to review military reports sent from the capital.

Lin Shuanghe sat nearby, watching him. After a while, he went out and quickly returned, carrying a plate of dried fruit, which he quietly placed on Xiao Jue’s table.

Xiao Jue glanced at him.

“The kitchen happened to make some today. Since you like them, have a bit more.”

Xiao Jue frowned. “What is this?”

“Plums!” Lin Shuanghe slapped his thigh, speaking earnestly. “Do you not like sour things? These are freshly picked and unprocessed—as sour as they come.”

After a moment of silence, Xiao Jue said, “Take it away.”

Lin Shuanghe straightened up, fanning himself as he said, “I am not leaving. Xiao Huaijin, even Chu Zilan has said so much—how can you still sit still? If you do not act soon, He Yan will be taken away by Chu Zilan sooner or later.”

The young man replied indifferently, “It has nothing to do with me.”

“You, me, and He Yan—we’ve faced life and death together in Jiyang City. Even if there’s no affection, there’s still loyalty. What kind of person Chu Zilan is, both of us know very well. As a fellow man, what he wants is obvious even to a fool. Chu Zilan cannot break free from Xu Pingting, yet he wants He Yan to pine for him. You do not know, but back when I was in Jiyang, He Yan was so lovesick over Chu Zilan that she told me she did not plan to marry in this lifetime. Tell me, what kind of sin has this man committed?”

Xiao Jue lowered his eyes, a flicker of emotion passing through them, but he did not stop Lin Shuanghe from continuing.

“He does not have the ability to marry her, yet he insists on provoking her. I think this man lacks integrity,” Lin Shuanghe said. “He Yan may be a bit naive, but she’s skilled, loyal, and quite good-looking. Apart from her ordinary family background, how is she inferior to anyone else? Such a fine girl should not be ruined by Chu Zilan. In Liangzhou Garrison, aside from me, you are the only one who can match Chu Zilan. Go and win He Yan’s heart back, and we can plan from there.”

Xiao Jue sneered, “What kind of person do you take me for?”

“I know this is unfair to you,” Lin Shuanghe patted his friend’s shoulder. “But think about it—if Chu Zilan continues to act so recklessly, trouble is bound to happen sooner or later. Can you say for sure that there are no people arranged by Xu Pingting around him? Once word gets back, He Yan will be in big trouble. I cannot stand by and do nothing, and neither can you. After all, you two pretended to be husband and wife once. A day as husband and wife brings a hundred days of affection—how can you be so heartless?”

This was getting more and more outrageous. Xiao Jue said, “If you keep spouting nonsense, I will have someone send you back to Shuojing tomorrow.”

Lin Shuanghe choked back his words, sighed, and said, “I’ve said all I needed to say. If you will not act, I will. I cannot just stand by and let He Yan be bullied by Xu Pingting for nothing.”

With that, he turned and left.

The room fell silent once more. Xiao Jue’s gaze fell on the plate of unripe plums on the table, and a wave of irritation suddenly washed over him. The brush in his hand snapped in two.

The next moment, a rustling sound came from the connecting door, followed by the click of the lock opening. Even though the door was already open, the person outside still pretended to knock politely: “Commander, may I come in?”

Xiao Jue: “…”

“If you do not say anything, I will take it as a yes,” the person said very naturally, pushing the door open. As soon as she entered, she met Xiao Jue’s icy gaze.

“Ahem.” He Yan straightened up. “Commander, you are in the room? Why did you not say anything? I thought you were not here.”

Xiao Jue: “What do you want?”

“I came to ask you,” He Yan said seriously, “During tomorrow’s training, should I follow today’s routine or stick to the previous one?”

Even though she had offended Xiao Jue and made him angry today, he was still her superior. He Yan had to swallow her pride and came to ask politely.

“If your stamina allows, you can increase it fivefold.”

Why did it sound like his anger had not subsided but was actually growing stronger? He Yan pondered, feeling it would be wiser not to provoke Xiao Jue today, so she nodded. “I understand. Then, Commander, rest early. I have matters to attend to and will not disturb you any longer.” With that, she prepared to leave.

“You are very busy?” Xiao Jue scoffed. “What matters?”

“Fourth Young Master Chu asked me to go see him tonight, saying he has something very important to tell me,” He Yan replied. “It should be about time.”

She spoke with unease. In truth, He Yan had no idea what Chu Zhao wanted with her. When Ying Xiang came to deliver the message, she had been solemn and earnest, making it impossible to take the matter lightly.

Xiao Jue lifted his gaze to look at her.

Under the lamplight, the young commander’s face was breathtakingly handsome. His inner robe hung loosely, his skin as smooth as jade, yet his eyes were like a frozen pond that had endured three winters—sharp and intimidating enough to make one shrink back.

His voice, however, remained calm, carrying a trace of barely perceptible anger.

“You are not allowed to go.”

CONTENT END 165

chapters.title: Chapter 166. Official Appointment.
chapters.content:
“You are not allowed to go.”

He Yan froze.

A moment later, she asked, “Why?”

Xiao Jue looked at her, his lips curling slightly, his tone as mocking as ever. “Chu Zilan is Xu Jingfu’s man. He has ulterior motives for staying at Liangzhou Garrison. If you get too close to a spy, are you also planning to pledge allegiance to Xu Jingfu?”

This accusation was a serious one. He Yan quickly denied it. “I am not, I haven’t!”

Xiao Jue snorted coldly and ignored her.

“General Xiao, of course, I know Fourth Young Master Chu’s identity is special,” He Yan said with utmost sincerity. “I promise, the things we discuss in private never involve any secrets about Liangzhou Garrison. Besides, I do not even know any secrets about Liangzhou Garrison. If Fourth Young Master Chu truly intends to probe military affairs, I will avoid the topic.” In her past life, she had been particularly sensitive in this regard, so Xiao Jue really did not need to worry about it.

“Moreover,” He Yan added, “if he truly has ulterior motives at Liangzhou Garrison, getting close to him like this might actually allow me to extract some information, which could be beneficial for us.”

Xiao Jue glanced at her. “You are so foolish that you will likely be exposed before you can extract anything.”

He Yan: “…”

Perhaps Jiang Jiao was wrong. It was not just women—men also had days each month when they were extremely irritable and found fault with everyone.

Since Xiao Jue would not let her go today, no matter what, He Yan sighed inwardly and said, “Alright, General Xiao, I will not go to see him. But I should at least inform the maid from Fourth Young Master Chu’s side. Otherwise, breaking the promise without any explanation would not be good.”

Ying Xiang had spoken with such seriousness when she came earlier—she hoped it was not truly an urgent matter.

Xiao Jue’s expression remained calm. “No need. You will not be interacting with him in the future anyway.”

He Yan: “…”

Xiao Jue was truly direct in his dealings.

…

Night deepened. Ying Xiang entered from outside, closed the door, and walked over to the man by the window, lowering her voice. “Fourth Young Master, the light in Young Lady He’s room has gone out. She must have retired for the night.”

Upon hearing this, Chu Zhao showed no anger, only shaking his head with a faint smile. “As expected.”

“It must be because General Xiao forbade it,” Ying Xiang said. “But to break the promise without even a word of explanation is truly…”

“It’s fine.” Chu Zhao turned to look at the thrush in the birdcage hanging by the window. In this harsh, cold land, it added a touch of color because of him, as if bringing back the bustling atmosphere of Shuojing. He played with the bird for a while before turning around and saying, “The more nervous Xiao Huaijin is, the more it proves one thing.”

“He Yan is very different to him.”

The lamplight on the table flickered gently, and his voice faded into the shadows along with it.

“She will become Xiao Huaijin’s weakness.”

…

The next day, He Yan went to the martial arts field for daily training as usual. Xiao Jue was also present today. Given his unusually erratic mood over the past few days, He Yan did not dare slack off and trained with extra effort. Around noon, just as it was almost time for a break, Shen Han and a few others suddenly rushed over from the Liangzhou Garrison recruits’ side, running up to Xiao Jue and saying, “Commander, Commander, someone has arrived from the capital!”

The voice was loud enough that the Southern Garrison Troops remained unmoved, but He Yan found it strange. Why would someone from the capital came to Liangzhou Garrison out of the blue? Ever since they drove away the Wutu people led by Rida Muzi, Liangzhou Garrison had enjoyed peace for over half a year. For someone to come from the capital at this time, could something major have happened?

Xiao Jue instructed Tian Lang to continue drilling the new recruits while he followed Shen Han toward the other side. After a while, Shen Han and Xiao Jue reappeared, trailed by a large group of people. At the forefront was a eunuch dressed in palace robes, holding a horsetail whisk and wearing a kindly smile. Xiao Jue signaled to Tian Lang, who immediately ordered the Southern Garrison Troops to halt their daily training.

The amiable-looking eunuch stepped forward and said with a smile, “Which one is He Yan?”

He Yan, hearing her name called, was taken aback. She stepped forward and bowed. “I am, sir.”

The eunuch looked He Yan up and down, his gaze unsettling. This scene was not unfamiliar to He Yan—she had experienced it before. Her heart raced with sudden surprise. Could it be…?

In the next moment, the eunuch announced, “His Majesty has issued a decree. Young Master He, receive the imperial edict.”

He Yan knelt respectfully as the man before her unrolled a bright yellow scroll and proclaimed in a drawn-out voice, “By the Mandate of Heaven, the Emperor decrees: He Yan of the Liangzhou Garrison, loyal and courageous, skilled in battle, has repeatedly distinguished himself in the Wutu campaign, greatly pleasing Our heart. He is hereby conferred the title of Lord Wu’an, with ceremonial robes and regalia. Let this be proclaimed throughout the land. So it is decreed—”

He Yan was stunned. Lord Wu’an?

Seeing her motionless, the eunuch reminded her, “Young Master He? Hurry and receive the edict to express your gratitude.”

He Yan quickly stepped forward, kowtowed, and accepted the decree. Yet her mind was still filled with doubt. Why would the Emperor reward her at this critical moment? On the surface, it seemed to be for her contributions in the recent Wutu and Jiyang campaigns involving the Liangzhou Garrison. But how did the palace learn of this? Xiao Jue would not have spoken of it, and even if Mu Hongjin had reported the events truthfully, the Emperor would hardly have taken notice of such a minor figure—especially since she was not the main protagonist in these two battles.

Before her doubts could fully settle, the eunuch clasped his hands and congratulated her with a smile. “Congratulations, congratulations! Young Master He is so talented and accomplished at such a young age. Your future is bound to be limitless.”

He Yan smiled and returned the courtesy, then glanced at Xiao Jue, who was frowning slightly, seemingly not entirely pleased with the situation. He Yan understood—this matter must have taken Xiao Jue by surprise as well.

The arrival of people from the capital was not solely for the purpose of rewarding her. The main focus was on rewarding Xiao Jue, the commanding general. Chests of rewards were carried into the Liangzhou Garrison. The Southern Garrison Troops, disciplined and strict, dared not look sideways. The new recruits of the Liangzhou Garrison, however, had never witnessed such a spectacle. They eagerly craned their necks on the martial arts field, straining to hear what was happening.

When Xiao Jue followed the palace officials into the guard headquarters to speak, the new recruits of the Liangzhou Garrison swarmed around He Yan, crowding her in the center and showering her with congratulations.

“Congratulations, Brother He! You got promoted so quickly!”

“Does this mean you will not be staying with us in the Liangzhou Garrison anymore? You will go to the capital! To the capital! Hey, does anyone know what rank Lord Wu’an is? Is it higher than an instructor? If so, will the instructor have to call you ‘Big Brother’ from now on?”

“I always said Brother He was extraordinary. The first time I saw him, I knew he was no ordinary person. It was only a matter of time before he rose to prominence.”

“Pah, stop with the hindsight!”

The crowd pressed in so tightly that He Yan could not get a word in edgewise. Seeing the situation turning chaotic, Hong Shan pulled her out of the throng, and they sprinted away. Only when they reached the riverside, where the crowd thinned, and Xiao Mai and the others caught up, did He Yan finally find a moment to breathe.

“Brother He, congratulations!” Hong Shan laughed heartily. “You’ve finally achieved your wish.”

“You’ve already completed half the journey to making a name for yourself,” Huang Xiong said, twisting the prayer beads around his neck. “That’s quite fast.”

“What kind of dogshit luck is this?” Wang Ba said, rather unwillingly. “What kind of bewitching potion did you feed the higher-ups?”

Jiang Jiao smiled. “This is something Brother He earned step by step himself. In a place like Jiyang, one misstep could cost your life. Since he risked everything, the rewards he’s received now are well-deserved.”

“But,” Xiao Mai looked at He Yan, “why does Brother He seem not very happy?”

Everyone turned to He Yan. Back when they were competing for flags in Liangzhou Garrison, He Yan had acted as if she could not wait to join the Jiuqi Battalion and make her mark. Now that she’d actually been appointed an official position, there was no trace of joy on her face—instead, there was even a hint of worry.

Shitou asked, “What’s wrong?”

He Yan forced a smile. “It’s nothing; I just… cannot quite believe it.”

“Hah,” Wang Ba sneered. “This is like a beggar finding money—he’s so happy he’s gone mad. What’s there to be unhappy about? So pretentious!”

He Yan did not say anything. In fact, she was not exactly unhappy, just somewhat puzzled. Precisely because in her previous life as “He Rufei,” she had earned her achievements step by step through her own efforts, she knew how difficult promotion was. Now, being inexplicably and suddenly appointed as an official was truly unreasonable. And, of all things, it was the position of Lord Wu’an.

It was hard not to think too much about it.

Perhaps she should go ask Xiao Jue what exactly was going on behind the scenes.

…

After speaking with Hong Shan and the others, He Yan planned to go back and find Xiao Jue to clarify what had happened.

Before she reached her quarters, she saw Shen Muxue and Xiao Jue in the courtyard in front of the house. The two stood under a tree, with Shen Muxue saying something to Xiao Jue. After a while, Shen Muxue bent down and picked up a bolt of silk from a box on the ground. Among the rewards bestowed by the emperor were probably precious fabrics. Unfortunately, Xiao Jue had no family, and in Liangzhou Garrison, Shen Muxue was the only woman, so these clothing materials naturally went to her.

Shen Muxue seemed very happy, holding the silk and thanking Xiao Jue. Ever since He Yan had met Shen Muxue, this girl had always been cold and distant, like an unapproachable fairy. But now, seeing her smiling so radiantly at Xiao Jue made He Yan’s steps falter. Her legs felt as heavy as lead, making it difficult to take another step forward.

Hesitating, she decided to wait until the two had finished speaking before approaching. Unexpectedly, a voice sounded beside her ear: “Why are you not going over?”

He Yan turned around to see Chu Zhao standing before her, looking at her with some confusion.

“It’s not too urgent. It is fine to wait a bit before going over,” He Yan replied evasively. “Brother Chu, why are you here?”

“I came looking for you,” Chu Zhao said, glancing at the two under the tree and then at He Yan. “Since Brother He is not in a hurry, why not attend to my matter first?”

He Yan thought for a moment and said, “Alright.”

She turned and walked with Chu Zhao in the opposite direction from Xiao Jue, asking, “Brother Chu, is there something urgent you need from me?”

“It seems Brother He is truly very busy with daily training, so busy that you’ve forgotten the agreement we made last night and still have not remembered it now.”

He Yan suddenly realized that she had actually remembered it earlier today, but once the imperial decree from the capital arrived, she had completely forgotten about Chu Zhao’s matter. Hearing this, she apologized, “I am sorry; I accidentally fell asleep last night. I originally intended to come and apologize to you today, but…”

“Just a joke; do not take it to heart,” Chu Zhao smiled. “You received an official promotion today; of course, you should be happy.”

He Yan paused in her steps. “You already know?”

“I knew yesterday.”

Seeing He Yan’s puzzled expression, Chu Zhao explained, “The messenger from the capital sent me a carrier pigeon message yesterday, saying they would arrive today. I came to find you last night precisely to discuss this matter. I thought that since you were suddenly being promoted, it would be better to give you a heads-up in advance so you would not be caught off guard. I did not expect you to be asleep. But seeing how calm you are even after the promotion, it seems I worried for nothing.”

“You are saying the messenger from the capital sent you a carrier pigeon message yesterday?” He Yan looked at him. “Why would they inform you?”

Even Xiao Jue probably had not received the news in advance.

“Because,” Chu Zhao met her gaze and smiled gently, “I was the one who petitioned His Majesty to promote you.”

It was him?

Even though He Yan had considered many possibilities, she never expected this one. She could only ask, “Why did you do this, Brother Chu?”

Chu Zhao continued walking forward, speaking softly, “In Jiyang City, both of us witnessed firsthand the brutality of the Wutu soldiers. By the canal, you gave me the fire- and water-resistant clothing, for which I am deeply grateful. War is cruel, yet you showed no fear. Your bravery and courage are evident to me. Moreover, I had also heard about your fierce battle with Rida Muzi before this. For Great Wei to have a hero like you is a blessing.”

“I do not know why General Xiao refused to promote you, but I thought, if I could help you ‘achieve merit and build a career,’ I would be more than willing to assist.”

These words sounded perfectly reasonable, yet for some reason, He Yan still felt uneasy. After a moment of thought, she said, “But Brother Chu, your actions truly surprise me.”

“You do not seem particularly happy about the promotion?” he asked.

“I am just a bit overwhelmed for the moment.”

Chu Zhao looked at her, then, after a pause, smiled. “I thought you would be very happy. After all, with this promotion, you are one step closer to General Xiao. Since you like him, you no longer have to worry about the difference in status.”

He Yan nearly choked on her own saliva and stared at Chu Zhao in shock. “What did you say?”

“Does not Brother He like General Xiao?” Chu Zhao smiled warmly, touching his nose. “Otherwise, you would not have been so upset just now when you saw Physician Shen and General Xiao together.”

“I wasn’t,” He Yan instinctively denied.

Chu Zhao smiled without pressing further, yet he did not dismiss her words either. For a moment, He Yan felt deeply frustrated, wondering if she had missed many subtle details over time. How was it that everyone seemed to see it so clearly—Liu Buwang, Lin Shuanghe, and even Chu Zhao?

Had she been that obvious? She had always been restrained, polite, and careful.

Chu Zhao looked into the distance. “Actually, General Xiao might not be indifferent to you either. After all, given his temperament, he has shown you considerable care.”

He Yan asked, “You think so?”

“If Brother He wishes to know General Xiao’s true feelings, it is actually quite simple,” Chu Zhao said with a smile. “I can help you test him.”

“How would you test him?” He Yan was baffled.

The man before her suddenly leaned in. He Yan, who had been leaning against a tree, nearly threw a punch out of reflex as he drew close. His face stopped just short of hers, his gaze smiling and particularly intoxicating. “It’s simple. Brother He is a woman, so you may not understand a man’s possessiveness. If I deliberately act very close to you, and if General Xiao truly cares for you, he will surely become very angry. If he remains indifferent… then you need not waste any more effort on him, so it is a very straightforward method.”

He Yan silently repeated his words in her mind before grasping his meaning. When it came to military strategy, she could recite the Thirty-Six Stratagems backward and forward, but this kind of emotional maneuvering was something she had never encountered before. She immediately asked, “… According to you, would not this be taking advantage of you?”

Chu Zhao continued to look at her with a smile, his gaze unbearably gentle. “If it is for Brother He, being taken advantage of does not matter.”

These words were truly touching.

However…

He Yan straightened up and took a step to the side, avoiding his approaching chest. “Thank you for your kindness, Brother Chu, but I do not wish to do this.”

A flicker of surprise passed through Chu Zhao’s eyes. “Why?”

“I think I understand what you mean. But when it comes to matters of the heart, how can we mix in schemes? Whether I confess my feelings openly or keep them hidden for a lifetime, I want to be honest and straightforward. If I have to exhaust myself with tests and guesses, would that not be exhausting? Even if I gained such a relationship, it would not be what I truly desire. Have you not heard the saying, Brother Chu? Using lies to test lies only leads to more lies. In the end, I would not know what was real and what was false.”

He Yan did not voice the rest of her thoughts: Xiao Jue disliked Chu Zhao intensely. Even if Xiao Jue did not care for her, seeing her with Chu Zhao would still provoke his anger. If she misinterpreted that as jealousy, would she not just be deluding herself?

Chu Zhao was momentarily stunned. “Are you not curious, Brother He, about what place you hold in General Xiao’s heart?”

“Not curious.”

He Yan answered so briskly that Chu Zhao was left speechless for a moment.

“Fourth Young Master Chu, I never intended for him to know,” He Yan said. “And I do not plan for him to know in the future either. So, I appreciate your kindness.”

“You do not want to be with him?”

“Things in this world change in the blink of an eye. The word ‘together,’ Fourth Young Master Chu, can only be certain for a moment, not a lifetime. And all I can be certain of is my own heart.”

Chu Zhao looked at He Yan, his lips moving as if he wanted to say something, but in the end, he remained silent. After a moment, he regained his earlier smile. “Since it is Brother He’s wish, I will not presume to act on my own. However, my offer still stands. If one day you change your mind and wish to ‘use’ me, I will not refuse in the slightest.”

He Yan also smiled, her tone particularly firm. “That day will never come.”

…

As He Yan’s figure gradually faded into the distance, Ying Xiang stepped out of the house and said softly, “Fourth Young Master.”

Chu Zhao looked at his empty hands and clicked his tongue. “She actually refused.”

“Young Lady He does not intend to let General Xiao know her feelings,” Ying Xiang sighed. “She does not want to put General Xiao in a difficult position.”

Chu Zhao smiled faintly. “There are actually such foolish women in this world. They neither strive for what they want nor seek to stay together, clinging to feelings that are invisible and intangible, yet believing them to be the noblest thing in the world. Ridiculous.”

This reminded him of Ye Runmei, who was the same. Women who sacrifice themselves for love were all equally foolish and deserving of contempt.

Ying Xiang lowered her gaze and remained silent. After a long while, she heard Chu Zhao say, “Let’s go.”

…

He Yan slowly made her way back.

She never expected that it was actually Chu Zhao who had petitioned Emperor Wenxuan to grant her an official position. The reasons Chu Zhao gave her sounded perfectly reasonable. If He Yan were truly a clueless new recruit, suddenly receiving such an appointment would likely send her into raptures. Any previous prejudices or suspicions she held toward Chu Zhao would instantly vanish, and she might even blame herself for judging a gentleman with a petty heart.

But she was no ordinary, ignorant soldier. As a member of the Flying Swan, she was well-versed in military affairs and leadership. Therefore, He Yan understood better than anyone that the title of Wu Anlang was merely an honorary position with no real authority. It sounded impressive—a fourth-rank title, all flowery and grand—but in reality, it held no power to command troops. In her previous life, she had relied on no one, starting as a new recruit and having to sell countless merits to her superiors just to earn a minor position. Only through gradual promotions, until no one could overshadow her achievements, did she finally gain the emperor’s recognition. But now, though it seemed like she had soared to the skies in one step, she actually wielded less authority than a centurion.

If Chu Zhao had merely petitioned the emperor, leaving the specific appointment to His Majesty’s discretion, that would have been one thing. But if the title of Lord Wu’an was personally proposed by Chu Zhao, the implications ran much deeper.

He had petitioned for her appointment, yet requested a position with no real authority. What exactly was he scheming?

…

In the room, Fei Nu and Lin Shuanghe stood, looking at the figure by the window.

“My Sister He has been appointed?” Lin Shuanghe was utterly confused. “Did you not say you would petition the emperor after returning to Shuojing? What’s going on?”

“Young Master Lin,” Fei Nu could not help but interject, “this time, it was Fourth Young Master Chu who petitioned the emperor.”

“Chu Zilan?” Lin Shuanghe frowned. “What does my Sister He’s appointment have to do with him? What kind of favor is he trying to curry?”

Xiao Jue’s expression remained calm, though upon closer inspection, a hint of coldness flickered in his eyes.

Fei Nu sighed. “It’s not about currying favor or not. Being appointed now is not a good thing.”

Lin Shuanghe paused in fanning himself, glancing at Fei Nu and then at Xiao Jue. “What do you mean by that? I am not quite following.”

“I originally intended to petition for her appointment under her true identity as a woman after returning to the capital,” Xiao Jue said calmly. “Chu Zilan preempted me. On the surface, he appears to have helped He Yan, but in reality, he has planted a hidden danger.”

“One day, if He Yan’s identity is exposed, it will be considered deceiving the emperor—a crime punishable by death and the extermination of nine clans.”

Lin Shuanghe gasped sharply.

He stammered, “N-no way. Chu Zilan already knows about my Sister He’s identity as a woman? It has been kept secret for so long… Surely it will not be exposed in the future, right?”

“That’s precisely where Chu Zilan’s brilliance lies,” Xiao Jue sneered. “What he truly wants to deal with is me.”

He Yan was merely a tool to be used. Chu Zhao indeed kept He Yan’s secret, not announcing her identity to the world. Instead, he turned around and petitioned for her to be granted a title, successfully turning her identity into a trap. Without this incident, on the day He Yan’s identity as a woman was exposed, she could have found various excuses to deal with it. But after the emperor rewarded and promoted her, it became different.

He Yan would become the sharpest blade, piercing straight into Xiao Jue’s heart.

This was Chu Zilan’s plan.

CONTENT END 166

chapters.title: Chapter 167. A Bitter Victory.
chapters.content:
The door was right before her. He Yan hesitated for a moment but ultimately did not head straight into her own room. Instead, she walked to Xiao Jue’s door and knocked lightly.

After a while, Xiao Jue’s voice came from inside: “Come in.”

The door was unlocked. He Yan pushed it open and peeked inside. There was no one else in the room, only Xiao Jue standing there. He had already changed into his inner garments, likely preparing to rest. He Yan hesitated for a moment. “Commander, are you about to retire for the night?”

“What is it?”

He Yan entered the room and closed the door behind her. She walked in but suddenly found herself at a loss for words. After a brief pause, she looked at Xiao Jue. “I’ve been promoted to Lord Wu’an, Commander. What is going on?”

“What is going on?” Xiao Jue said coldly. “Did Chu Zilan not tell you?”

He actually guessed it. He Yan took a step forward. “Commander, you know it was Fourth Young Master Chu who petitioned for my promotion.”

Xiao Jue’s gaze fixed on her face, a faint, cold smile curling his lips. “You two seem to be on very good terms.”

“No, Commander, you are wronging me,” He Yan protested. “I only found out today that Fourth Young Master Chu petitioned for my promotion. I am puzzled myself—why would he do such a thing out of the blue?”

“Was it not because he saw you stagnating under my command and felt indignant on your behalf, so he personally submitted a petition for your promotion?” Xiao Jue turned around, hanging Yinqiu on the wall, his voice laced with sarcasm. “Young Lady He is quite popular, more so than one might expect.”

Why did his words sound so mocking? He Yan frowned. “I did not ask for this, Commander. You cannot just take your anger out on me.”

“I’ve said it before.” Xiao Jue’s expression turned stern. “Whether you like Chu Zilan is your business, but in Liangzhou Garrison, getting close to a spy is my business.”

His words were harsh, as if she were a traitor colluding with outsiders. He Yan thought to herself that Xiao Jue’s temper was inexplicable, even worse than Shen Muxue’s. The frustration that had built up over the past two days surged within her, and she could not help but retort, “Fourth Young Master Chu and I are just ordinary friends. We are not particularly close. Commander, are you not close to Physician Shen? Do you not have people you are friendly with, too?”

“Friendly?” Xiao Jue stared at her and slowly repeated the word. After a moment, he laughed, but there was no warmth in his eyes. “It seems Chu Zilan has managed to please you quite well.”

He Yan replied, “Whether he pleases me or not, I do not know. But at least Fourth Young Master Chu is not as unreasonable as you, Commander.”

Xiao Jue said coldly, “Young Lady He is free to seek out someone who is not unreasonable.”

He Yan: “…”

She usually had a good temper and considered herself broad-minded. But over the past two days, she had already been unsettled by the matter with Shen Muxue. Now, seeing Xiao Jue’s aggressive attitude, her anger flared up. In that moment, she even forgot what she had originally wanted to ask Xiao Jue. Without another word, she turned and left. As she left, she nearly slammed the door but remembered that Xiao Jue was still her superior and restrained herself, closing the door properly before leaving with a defiant air.

The room fell silent once more.

After a while, Xiao Jue looked toward the door again. It was already closed. The visitor had arrived cautiously but left in a huff. The tense atmosphere from earlier seemed to linger in the air.

The young man’s expression turned cold. With a sudden wave of his hand, the oil lamp on the table extinguished, plunging everything into silence.

It was truly an unpleasant night.

…

Ever since that unpleasant parting with Xiao Jue, He Yan had thrown herself into daily training with renewed determination. She no longer sneaked over to Xiao Jue’s quarters every night to chat as she used to. For one thing, Xiao Jue’s attitude that day had been too harsh. It was Chu Zhao who had recommended her for the promotion, not her own request. She was already wary of Chu Zhao herself, yet Xiao Jue had taken his anger out on her, making it sound as though she were a spy, which infuriated He Yan. For another, as if cursed by some strange twist of fate, she had been unaware of Shen Muxue’s identity before, but now that she knew, she kept running into Xiao Jue and Shen Muxue together every few days.

It was only then that He Yan realized the exquisite pastries and meals in the food basket delivered to Xiao Jue’s room every day were all prepared by Shen Muxue. This young woman was not only skilled in poetry but also capable of following Xiao Jue to the distant frontier. Even in matters of daily life, she was meticulous and attentive. Seeing her display such virtuous qualities day after day, He Yan asked herself: if she were Xiao Jue, she would surely be moved.

The more she thought about it, the more disheartened she felt. She decided it was better to avoid seeing them altogether. By exhausting all her energy in the martial arts field every day and collapsing into sleep as soon as she returned to her room, the days became much more bearable.

However, her strained relationship with Xiao Jue did not go unnoticed. One day, as He Yan was leaving the martial arts field and heading back after dinner with Hong Shan and the others, Lin Shuanghe caught up with her.

“Brother He!” he greeted her naturally, waving as he approached. “Lately, I’ve been thinking how vast the Liangzhou Garrison is—even more so than the capital. Otherwise, how could I go days without catching a glimpse of you? If I had not run into you today, I’d have wondered if you’d returned to the capital.”

He Yan fell silent for a moment before replying, “I’ve been busy with daily training lately and have not had the chance to speak with you, Brother Lin. Please do not take it to heart.”

Lin Shuanghe fanned himself lightly, studying her with a knowing smile. “I am not that petty. But, Sister He,” he lowered his voice, “you and Huaijin had a fight, did you not? Usually, whenever I visited him, you were there half the time. These past few days, when I went to see him, tsk tsk, the lock on the connecting door was practically rusted shut. How long has it been since you last sat in his room?”

He Yan glared coldly. “Sit? What’s there to sit for? I am not even that close to him!”

“So you really did quarrel?” Lin Shuanghe looked surprised. “You’ve always had such a good temper. How did you end up in a real argument with Xiao Huaijin?”

He Yan had been bottling up her frustration for days, and his question unleashed it. “How should I know what I did to offend him this time? Brother Lin, do you men also have those days every month where you find everyone irritating and just lash out for no reason, making a fuss over nothing?”

Lin Shuanghe stroked his chin thoughtfully. “I only know that women tend to be irritable and short-tempered during their monthly cycles. I was not aware that men experienced something similar. What kind of new ailment is this?” He then glanced sideways at He Yan. “Come, tell me, how exactly did Xiao Huaijin make a fuss over nothing?”

He Yan thought to herself that since Lin Shuanghe was Xiao Jue’s close friend, he must understand Xiao Jue better than she did. So she recounted the entire incident from beginning to end, concluding, “Brother Lin, do you not agree that this matter really is not my fault? The Commander only said those things because he already suspected me, not knowing how deeply it hurt me to hear such words when my loyalty lies entirely with the Liangzhou Garrison.”

Lin Shuanghe closed his fan, staring at He Yan without speaking, his gaze unusually strange. He Yan felt unnerved by his stare and frowned, asking, “Brother Lin?”

“Sister He,” Lin Shuanghe lowered his voice, “do you think Huaijin suspects you because you’ve been too close to Chu Zilan, and Chu Zilan might be a spy for the Liangzhou Garrison, which is why he’s acting this way?”

He Yan replied, “Exactly.”

“Then have you considered any other reasons?” Lin Shuanghe coaxed gently.

He Yan asked, “What reasons?”

“For example… do not view this matter from the perspective of a superior and subordinate, but rather from the relationship between a man and a woman. Then…” Lin Shuanghe lowered his voice even further, sounding particularly mysterious, “Could it be that Xiao Huaijin saw you getting too close to Chu Zilan and, as a man, felt jealous?”

The surroundings fell silent.

Lin Shuanghe observed He Yan’s expression.

After a long while, He Yan reached out to touch Lin Shuanghe’s forehead. “Brother Lin, are you ill? I think you should not stand here catching the wind but should go find Physician Shen for a check-up.”

Lin Shuanghe: “?”

“Look at me,” He Yan pointed at herself, “and then look at Physician Shen. Do you think the Commander would be jealous because of me?” He Yan continued, “I am afraid that in the Commander’s eyes, there’s no difference between me, you, and Instructor Shen. Perhaps he is jealous, but it is like a friend being taken away by someone else—it has nothing to do with romantic feelings.”

She spoke with such certainty that even the usually eloquent Lin Shuanghe was left speechless for a moment. After a while, he said, “What you said is not right. What do you mean by ‘look at you and Physician Shen’? I think you are wonderful. I’ve seen my fair share of flowers, and my words carry weight even in Shuojing.”

He Yan shook her head and smiled. “Am I prettier than Physician Shen?”

Lin Shuanghe: “Well…”

“Is my family background more distinguished than Physician Shen’s?”

“Uh…”

“Do I treat General Xiao like a precious treasure, willing to travel thousands of li just to fight alongside him?”

Lin Shuanghe: “…”

He struggled to refute, “You cannot put it that way. You have your own strengths.”

He Yan smiled. “Then tell me, Brother Lin, what are my strengths?”

Lin Shuanghe said, “You are generous! Loyal, righteous, and value friendship! You are skilled, straightforward, and bold, never coy. You are passionate, resilient, and can fight in battles. Are these not strengths?”

He Yan looked at him. “Brother Lin, the strengths you mentioned—Instructor Shen has them, Chi Wu and Fei Nu have them, and most of the new recruits in the Liangzhou Garrison are like this too. Does that mean the Commander admires and appreciates them all?”

Lin Shuanghe could not respond to that.

He suddenly felt a wave of exhaustion. Originally, he had wanted to help his friend test this girl’s feelings, but now, forget testing—He Yan refused to believe that Xiao Jue had any special affection for her. How could he even continue? This girl seemed as bright and cheerful as a little sun, yet deep down, why was she so insecure? It was as if she had never been treated well, unwilling to believe even the slightest hint of being “favored.”
